passages: Apple has had a busy fall, with the launch of the iPhone Duo, HomeView smart hub, and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio.
But there’s one more event this week, and it might be the biggest of all.
And you can follow every rumor and announcement with us right here.

While the iPad mini has all the makings of a pro device, with an OLED display, A20 Pro processor, and refined color palette, but it’s still missing one major feature of Apple’s other Pro devices: 120Hz ProMotion.
There were scattered reports that Apple would be bringing the high-end screen tech to the mini along with its OLED upgrade, but alas, it didn’t make the cut.
Looks like we’ll have to wait another 2-3 years.
That’s a bunch of firsts for a non-Pro iPad and a massive upgrade.
The screen is now 8.5 inches (up from 8.3 inches) and the camera is now on the landscape edge.
It also got a price hike, but not as bad as feared: $699.
That probably means we’re getting the M6 iMac and M6 MacBook Pro tomorrow and the touchscreen MacBook Pro on Wednesday.
So even if you’re not planning on buying something new this week, you devices can get some new features at least.
Apple has hidden a pretty nice upgrade in the tech specs.
But if you opt for the 512GB model you get the full version of the chip, with a 6-core CPU and a dual 16-core Neural Engine.
Since Apple has only announced one day of announcements, one of three things could happen today: An iPad mini announcement at 9 am ET, 1 pm ET, or nothing at all.
iPad owners (with the exception of iPad Pro owners, who are a whole different breed) tend not to worry too much about tech specs.
How will Apple sell its new touchscreen Mac to the public?
According to Mark Gurman , it will be billed as an “optional” feature rather than a primary one, not unlike the Touch Bar.
But I would argue that cutting-edge AI performance is a pretty low priority for most of the mini’s prospective customers.
This week could see Apple add a third entry to that list.

extraction.body: Apple has had a busy fall, with the launch of the iPhone Duo, HomeView smart hub, and the M5 Ultra Mac Studio. But there’s one more event this week, and it might be the biggest of all. And you can follow every rumor and announcement with us right here. Apple kicked off its week of releases with the new iPad mini , which got a thinner design, new A20 Pro chip, and an OLED display. As you can guess by the thinly veiled pun, this week’s marquee announcement is a new MacBook Pro, but not just any MacBook Pro. Here’s what else we’re expecting to see: Touchscreen MacBook Pro: After years of denials, Apple appears to be on the verge of releasing its first-ever touchscreen MacBook . Rumors say it will have a new design with a lighter chassis, Dynamic Island, and an OLED display. And a very high price tag. M6 iMac: Apple announced the M6 chip in the Mac mini last month and now it’ll reportedly make its way into the iMac . There could be new colors too. M6 MacBook Pro: The entry-level MacBook Pro gets its annual chip-and-ship upgrade. With two more days of annoucements coming this week, we want to know what you’re planning to buy: an iPad mini, M6 iMac, M6 MacBook Pro, or touchscreen MacBook Pro. Readers are weighing in and there’s no surprise here, with 41 percent of the vote, the touchscreen MacBook Pro leads the pack. Join the conversation and take our poll online . Following this weekend’s iPhone Duo hinge issues , which has led to numerous cracked and damaged screens, Mark Gurman reports that Apple will be putting emphasis on the MacBook Pro’s new hinge when the touchscreen model arrives this week. extraction.body: A new iPad Mini and possible upgrades to the MacBook Pro and iMac are coming. Here's what we're anticipating in another big week for Apple. Apple’s Pro and Tell experience week is here, and it’s already off to a strong start, with the new iPad Mini unveiled on Monday morning. But there’s more to come: We’re also expecting refreshes and changes to the iMac and MacBook Pro lineups, including a long-anticipated touchscreen laptop . Apple’s had a busy few months, launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 , Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the AirPods 5 , followed by the iPhone Duo launch at the end of last week. Apple’s smart home lineup , revealed during its recent Welcome Home event, is up next: the HomePod Mini 2 will launch on Friday; the Apple HomeView and Apple TV 4K on Nov. 13; and availability for the Home Collection products begins in December. This week will culminate with Apple hosting a special event on Wednesday, and CNET will be on the ground capturing all the latest details. But ahead of that, here’s what we’re expecting to see from the tech giant, and we’ll update this piece as more details are revealed. Announced on Monday, Apple’s new iPad Mini is available to preorder on Wednesday and will go on sale Nov. 6. It starts at $699 for 128GB of storage, $799 for 256GB and $999 for 512GB. Setting it apart from the last iPad Mini , which came out two years ago, the new tablet has an 8.5-inch OLED screen (versus an LCD), IP67 water and dust resistance, an Apple A20 processor, a repositioned front-facing camera and a through-screen speaker system called Acoustic Display, as well as being thinner and lighter than before. We don’t yet know what’s coming for the rest of this week, but one heavily rumored product is a new iMac , which we’re expecting to be updated with an M6 chip, just like the Mac Mini. The current generation of iMac was last updated in 2024. It’s likely the new iMac will be announced Tuesday morning. We’re anticipating several MacBook Pro updates this week, including an OLED touchscreen version. “I’m expecting a 14-inch MacBook Pro to get updated with the M6 chip,” CNET Managing Editor Josh Goldman says. “I’m not sure the 16-inch will get that, since it usually doesn’t get a base M-series chip. My feeling is they’ll probably hold off on that until next year, when they can add the M6 Pro/Max chips.” Goldman added that he’s expecting the 14- and 16-inch OLED touchscreen models will still be based on the M5 Pro/Max chips, however. The MacBook Pro chip upgrade announcement could hit Tuesday morning, to be followed on Wednesday by the new touchscreen versions of Apple’s highest-end laptop. And as for the iPhone Duo launch last week, check out CNET’s ongoing folding test — you can watch Day 1 of the livestream here and tune in on Tuesday as we continue testing how many times the iPhone Duo can fold without cracking in the CNET lab. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

extraction.body: It feels like Apple’s Welcome Home event just happened. Yet, the company is back with another launch, focused on the MacBook Pro, it looks like. Its “Pro and tell” event is scheduled for October 28th at 1PM ET. While obviously nothing is confirmed yet, it sure seems like we’re finally going to get that long-rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro. There could be an OLED update for the iPad Mini, plus M6 updates across other devices, following the M6 debut with the Mac Mini in August. A touchscreen MacBook Pro A MacBook Pro with an OLED touchscreen has been a fixture of the rumor mill since at least early 2023. The name MacBook Ultra has been floating around, but Apple is unlikely to rebrand its flagship laptop line. This will be the first touchscreen laptop and the first OLED laptop from Apple. It will supposedly feature an iPhone-esque Dynamic Island, but don’t expect a dramatic revamp of the macOS interface — The touchscreen MacBook isn’t going to be some sort of iPad hybrid. Instead, Apple may wait to upgrade its higher-end processors until it introduces the M7 next year. M6 MacBook Pro That doesn’t mean there won’t be an M6 MacBook Pro, however. The base model of the MacBook Pro could be getting a bump from the M5 after the M6 debuted in the Mac Mini earlier this year. Unfortunately, they’re also expected to come with a price increase as component shortages reverberate through the Apple lineup. M6 iMac The iMac is also expected to get an M6 update, nearly two years after its last revision. Apple’s all-in-one desktop appears like it’s going to skip right over the M5. Don’t expect any real changes beyond that, though. But at least we might get some new color options, just like we did with the M4 model. OLED iPad Mini Another long-rumored device that might finally be making its debut on Wednesday is the OLED iPad Mini. Other than the iPad Pro, the tablet lineup has stuck with LCDs until now. The new OLED iPad could kick off a broader transition for the product line. Otherwise, it likely won’t be a significant redesign, but expect a processor upgrade from the aging A17 to the A20 that debuted with the iPhone 18.

extraction.body: A new iPad Mini and possible upgrades to the MacBook Pro and iMac are coming. Here's what we're anticipating in another big week for Apple. Apple’s Pro and Tell experience week is here, and it’s already off to a strong start, with the new iPad Mini unveiled on Monday morning. But there’s more to come: We’re also expecting refreshes and changes to the iMac and MacBook Pro lineups, including a long-anticipated touchscreen laptop . Apple’s had a busy few months, launching the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max in September alongside the Apple Watch Series 12 , Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the AirPods 5 , followed by the iPhone Duo launch at the end of last week. Apple’s smart home lineup , revealed during its recent Welcome Home event, is up next: the HomePod Mini 2 will launch on Friday; the Apple HomeView and Apple TV 4K on Nov. 13; and availability for the Home Collection products begins in December. This week will culminate with Apple hosting a special event on Wednesday, and CNET will be on the ground capturing all the latest details. But ahead of that, here’s what we’re expecting to see from the tech giant, and we’ll update this piece as more details are revealed. Announced on Monday, Apple’s new iPad Mini is available to preorder on Wednesday and will go on sale Nov. 6. It starts at $699 for 128GB of storage, $799 for 256GB and $999 for 512GB. Setting it apart from the last iPad Mini , which came out two years ago, the new tablet has an 8.5-inch OLED screen (versus an LCD), IP67 water and dust resistance, an Apple A20 processor, a repositioned front-facing camera and a through-screen speaker system called Acoustic Display, as well as being thinner and lighter than before. We don’t yet know what’s coming for the rest of this week, but one heavily rumored product is a new iMac , which we’re expecting to be updated with an M6 chip, just like the Mac Mini. The current generation of iMac was last updated in 2024. It’s likely the new iMac will be announced Tuesday morning. We’re anticipating several MacBook Pro updates this week, including an OLED touchscreen version. “I’m expecting a 14-inch MacBook Pro to get updated with the M6 chip,” CNET Managing Editor Josh Goldman says. “I’m not sure the 16-inch will get that, since it usually doesn’t get a base M-series chip. My feeling is they’ll probably hold off on that until next year, when they can add the M6 Pro/Max chips.” Goldman added that he’s expecting the 14- and 16-inch OLED touchscreen models will still be based on the M5 Pro/Max chips, however. The MacBook Pro chip upgrade announcement could hit Tuesday morning, to be followed on Wednesday by the new touchscreen versions of Apple’s highest-end laptop. And as for the iPhone Duo launch last week, check out CNET’s ongoing folding test — you can watch Day 1 of the livestream here and tune in on Tuesday as we continue testing how many times the iPhone Duo can fold without cracking in the CNET lab. © 2026 CNET, a Ziff Davis company. All rights reserved.

Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system.
C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency.
6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit.
Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational.
A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks.
It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips.

3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering.

It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.
3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference.

Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.

“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”

At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1

The new iPad mini comes with a stunning OLED display that delivers amazing front-of-screen performance and an even larger 8.5-inch size while maintaining the same footprint as the previous mini, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. 2 The Super Retina XDR display features OLED technology to deliver pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery.

For an even better visual experience across a range of lighting conditions, iPad mini also features peak brightness of up to 1200 nits — more than 2x higher than the previous generation — and supports 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. And with a 1-nit minimum brightness, iPad mini is even more suitable for dim environments, from users reading in bed at night to pilots checking their electronic flight bag in the cockpit. iPad mini also offers a new nano-texture display option, which users love on iPad Pro, that reduces glare in bright environments — ideal for creatives editing outdoors or technicians working in the field. Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases.

A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3

The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. By engaging all 32 cores, A20 Pro becomes a powerhouse for more advanced on-device AI workloads. A20 Pro also brings over a 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth, unlocking additional performance for new levels of capability and responsiveness across graphics and AI-intensive workloads.
A Rich New Audio Experience and Advanced Cameras

The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.

The 12MP Center Stage front camera is now on the landscape edge, perfect for FaceTime calls, video conferencing, and collaboration. And the 12MP Wide back camera captures gorgeous photos with Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, while the addition of an Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and makes document scanning better than ever.

iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6

Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system. C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency. 6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit. Users can also enjoy the benefits of eSIM, which lets them quickly and securely add a new plan, connect and transfer existing plans digitally, and stay in touch with family and friends regardless of Wi-Fi availability. 7
iPadOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

iPad mini users can get even more done with Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. 4 iPad mini also supports Apple’s most advanced on-device model ever, for even more expressive voices with Siri AI as well as a major boost in accuracy with systemwide dictation.

Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend. And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery. In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates. Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy. When Private Cloud Compute is handling users’ requests, their personal data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference. With iPadOS 27.2, iPad mini also supports extended display mode when connected to an external display, great for users multitasking with windowed apps.

Additionally, powerful and easy-to-use tools help parents manage what their kids can see, who they can talk to, and when they have access to apps. For parents and families looking for more information on how to help create safer, more enriching digital experiences for their kids, Apple also has a website with details on the latest tools and how to get started using them.
Accessories That Unlock More Ways to Be Productive and Creative

The new Smart Folio features a two-panel architecture, offering a slim, lightweight cover that magnetically attaches to iPad mini. 8 Crafted with TechWoven fabric in navy blue and taupe to complement the iPad mini finishes, the Smart Folio has an adjustable design that gives users a greater range of motion, including new viewing angles, for enhanced versatility.

iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life. 8 Apple Pencil (USB-C) is a great value for everyday tasks like note-taking and sketching, while Apple Pencil Pro delivers industry-leading capabilities for the ultimate pencil experience. With Apple Pencil Pro, users can take advantage of innovative features like squeeze and barrel roll to work in entirely new ways, as well as utilize Find My support to help locate it when misplaced.

iPad mini was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain. It is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. extraction.body: Apple's smallest iPad now features an OLED display, as well as a thinner and lighter design. Customers can pre-order it starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6. The larger 8.5-inch OLED display (up slightly from the 8.3-inch screen used previously) is available with a nano-texture option, delivering higher contrast, reduced glare, and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini. The nano-texture display is a $100 upgrade option available for models with 256GB or 512GB of storage only. Unfortunately, Apple's tech specs do not mention ProMotion support, so it appear that a 120Hz refresh rate is not in the cards this time around. The AI-capable A20 Pro is built with TSMC's advanced 2nm process and has Neural Accelerators in each GPU core. Models with 128GB or 256GB of storage have a 5-core CPU, 7-core GPU, and a single 16-core Neural Engine, while configurations with 512GB of storage get a 6-core CPU, 7-core GPU, and a dual 16-core Neural Engine. Apple says the A20 Pro chip offers up to 60% faster CPU performance, up to 2.7× faster graphics performance, and up to 4.5× faster AI performance compared to the A17 Pro chip that powered the previous iPad mini. A new 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge makes the new camera even better for video calls, while the device's new Acoustic Display provides an improved better audio experience, while eliminating speaker holes. Faster wireless and cellular connectivity come along for the ride in the form of Apple's N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. "Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume," said Apple. passages: Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.
The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.
A nano-texture display option is also available.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash.

Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).
Audio has also been reworked through an Acoustic Display system, similar to Sony’s BRAVIA TVs which uses the entire panel to improve audio quality.
Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies.
Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.

The new iPad mini also measures just 5.4mm thin, making it the most portable version of the device yet; on the processing side, the iPad mini now comes with the A20 Pro chip, carried straight from the iPhone 18 Pro – so you get all the latest and greatest Apple has to offer this year in a slightly bigger format. The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.

Despite housing a larger 8.5-inch screen, the overall footprint remains the same as the previous generation, thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner. The Super Retina XDR OLED display brings deeper blacks and supports the Apple P3 wide color gamut, with peak brightness reaching up to 1,200 nits (more than twice that of the previous generation, Apple says), while full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content sits at 600 nits. A nano-texture display option is also available.

Audio has also been reworked through an Acoustic Display system, similar to Sony’s BRAVIA TVs which uses the entire panel to improve audio quality. Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies. Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash. Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).

Pre-orders for the new iPad mini open on 29 October 2026 via apple.com/my and the Apple Store app; units will begin arriving to customers and appear in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorised Resellers from 6 November 2026. The tablet is available in 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB configurations in Midnight and Starlight finishes. The Wi-Fi model starts at RM2,999 , while the Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at RM3,699 .

coreStoryFacts.text: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever
Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system.
C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency.
6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit.
Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational.
A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks.
It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips.

3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering.

It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.
3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life.

Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful.
Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend.
And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery.
In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates.
Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy.

extraction.body: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever. The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.” At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1 The new iPad mini comes with a stunning OLED display that delivers amazing front-of-screen performance and an even larger 8.5-inch size while maintaining the same footprint as the previous mini, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. 2 The Super Retina XDR display features OLED technology to deliver pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery. For an even better visual experience across a range of lighting conditions, iPad mini also features peak brightness of up to 1200 nits — more than 2x higher than the previous generation — and supports 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. And with a 1-nit minimum brightness, iPad mini is even more suitable for dim environments, from users reading in bed at night to pilots checking their electronic flight bag in the cockpit. iPad mini also offers a new nano-texture display option, which users love on iPad Pro, that reduces glare in bright environments — ideal for creatives editing outdoors or technicians working in the field. Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases. A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3 The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. By engaging all 32 cores, A20 Pro becomes a powerhouse for more advanced on-device AI workloads. A20 Pro also brings over a 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth, unlocking additional performance for new levels of capability and responsiveness across graphics and AI-intensive workloads. A Rich New Audio Experience and Advanced Cameras The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating. The 12MP Center Stage front camera is now on the landscape edge, perfect for FaceTime calls, video conferencing, and collaboration. And the 12MP Wide back camera captures gorgeous photos with Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, while the addition of an Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and makes document scanning better than ever. iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6 Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system. C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency. 6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit. Users can also enjoy the benefits of eSIM, which lets them quickly and securely add a new plan, connect and transfer existing plans digitally, and stay in touch with family and friends regardless of Wi-Fi availability. 7 iPadOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI iPad mini users can get even more done with Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. 4 iPad mini also supports Apple’s most advanced on-device model ever, for even more expressive voices with Siri AI as well as a major boost in accuracy with systemwide dictation. passages: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever
Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance

CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6.

“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”

At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1

The new iPad mini comes with a stunning OLED display that delivers amazing front-of-screen performance and an even larger 8.5-inch size while maintaining the same footprint as the previous mini, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. 2 The Super Retina XDR display features OLED technology to deliver pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery.

For an even better visual experience across a range of lighting conditions, iPad mini also features peak brightness of up to 1200 nits — more than 2x higher than the previous generation — and supports 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. And with a 1-nit minimum brightness, iPad mini is even more suitable for dim environments, from users reading in bed at night to pilots checking their electronic flight bag in the cockpit. iPad mini also offers a new nano-texture display option, which users love on iPad Pro, that reduces glare in bright environments — ideal for creatives editing outdoors or technicians working in the field. Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases.

A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3

The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. By engaging all 32 cores, A20 Pro becomes a powerhouse for more advanced on-device AI workloads. A20 Pro also brings over a 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth, unlocking additional performance for new levels of capability and responsiveness across graphics and AI-intensive workloads.
A Rich New Audio Experience and Advanced Cameras

The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.

The 12MP Center Stage front camera is now on the landscape edge, perfect for FaceTime calls, video conferencing, and collaboration. And the 12MP Wide back camera captures gorgeous photos with Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, while the addition of an Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and makes document scanning better than ever.

iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6

Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system. C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency. 6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit. Users can also enjoy the benefits of eSIM, which lets them quickly and securely add a new plan, connect and transfer existing plans digitally, and stay in touch with family and friends regardless of Wi-Fi availability. 7
iPadOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI

iPad mini users can get even more done with Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. 4 iPad mini also supports Apple’s most advanced on-device model ever, for even more expressive voices with Siri AI as well as a major boost in accuracy with systemwide dictation.

Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend. And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery. In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates. Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy. When Private Cloud Compute is handling users’ requests, their personal data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference. With iPadOS 27.2, iPad mini also supports extended display mode when connected to an external display, great for users multitasking with windowed apps.

Additionally, powerful and easy-to-use tools help parents manage what their kids can see, who they can talk to, and when they have access to apps. For parents and families looking for more information on how to help create safer, more enriching digital experiences for their kids, Apple also has a website with details on the latest tools and how to get started using them.
Accessories That Unlock More Ways to Be Productive and Creative

The new Smart Folio features a two-panel architecture, offering a slim, lightweight cover that magnetically attaches to iPad mini. 8 Crafted with TechWoven fabric in navy blue and taupe to complement the iPad mini finishes, the Smart Folio has an adjustable design that gives users a greater range of motion, including new viewing angles, for enhanced versatility.

iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life. 8 Apple Pencil (USB-C) is a great value for everyday tasks like note-taking and sketching, while Apple Pencil Pro delivers industry-leading capabilities for the ultimate pencil experience. With Apple Pencil Pro, users can take advantage of innovative features like squeeze and barrel roll to work in entirely new ways, as well as utilize Find My support to help locate it when misplaced.

iPad mini was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain. It is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.

Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.

sources.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce
passages: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.

CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.

While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.

sources.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700
passages: The iPhone Duo may be a bit of a risk right now , but there’s a new mid-size Apple touchscreen device that might do the job.
Starting at $699, the 8th-gen iPad mini price has gone up, but there are some big changes.
Higher memory speed also helps with on-device AI applications, but the Neural Engine is the primary factor.
Unfortunately, not all versions of the new iPad mini will be equally capable.
These versions will also have a slightly different CPU configuration, with five cores instead of six.
Apple claims this is the most significant update ever for the iPad mini line.
The 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display (up from 8.3 inches) moves on from the IPS technology of the last-gen device to adopt OLED.
That means dapper blacks and a much higher peak brightness—1,200 nits versus just 500 nits for the previous mini.
It can also manage 1-nit minimum brightness so as not to sear your retinas in a dark room.
There will also be a nano-textured matte display option.
The display experience on the new mini should be much more in line with what we’ve come to expect from Apple’s Pro-level devices.
Apple has retained the 12 MP cameras for the front and back of the tablet, but the front-facing one has changed location.
Rather than being on the short edge for portrait-orientation video calls, it’s now on the long edge.
That might take a little getting used to for those who frequently use their tablets for FaceTime.

extraction.body: Just as rumors last week suggested, the redesigned 8th-generation iPad Mini (2026) has arrived ahead of Apple's "Pro and Tell" event on Wednesday, October 28th. The refreshed pint-sized tablet features a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, an improved front-facing camera, and, for the first time on any iPad, IP67 water and dust resistance. The redesigned pint-sized tablet also features a less thick 5.4mm design and 24% thinner bezels. On the display front, the new 8.5-inch OLED screen offers 2x higher peak brightness at 1,200 nits (along with 1 nit minimum brightness), plus a nano-texture display option similar to recent iPad Pro releases. However, the new iPad Mini still doesn't feature a 120Hz ProMotion display and is locked to 60Hz. The 2024-released 7th-generation iPad Mini featured an 8.3-inch LCD screen with relatively thick bezels. The larger OLED panel should deliver deeper blacks, improved contrast, and more vibrant colors. At the same time, the tablet might also have worse battery life, since OLED panel technology consumes more power, though efficiency improvements in the A20 Pro could offset that. In the press release, Apple says that the new iPad Mini can hit 10 hours of battery life while watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi. Regarding the A20 Pro specifically, the chip features a 5-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, making it compatible with Apple's new Siri AI features, including the assistant's more expressive voice. It also has a 7-core GPU that delivers up to 2.7x faster graphics performance. Lastly, the 512GB model features a 6-core CPU. The tablet's front-facing camera has been upgraded to a 12-megapixel Center Stage shooter that sits on its landscape bezel edge. Other upgrades include the Acoustic Display, which Apple says features "specially designed woofers" that are "paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume." Lastly, the tablet features Apple's C2 cellular modem (if you opt for the cellular version), alongside its N1 wireless chip. Apple says the new iPad Mini will be available to pre-order on Wednesday, October 28th, starting at $700, with availability launching on November 6th. While the 8th-gen iPad Mini seems like a solid all-around upgrade thanks to the A20 Pro chip and the new OLED panel, it's a bit crazy that it starts at $700, especially since the last refresh in 2024 launched at $500 (which already felt pretty expensive). Later this week, Apple is expected to reveal a touch-screen MacBook Pro and the M6-powered MacBook Pro and iPad. New features include more accurate health tracking and longer battery life.

The new tablet also gains an updated A20 Pro processor, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a nano-texture option for the display. It starts at $699, $100 more than the previous version, and will be available for pre-order on Oct. 28. Apple has been slow to update the iPad mini over the years, much to the chagrin of its niche yet vocal fanbase . The previous generation came out in 2024, adding more storage, Apple Pencil support and a processor upgrade. The version before that came out in 2021 and finally removed the aging Home button from the tiny tablet. Apple has spent more time updating other iPad models, including the entry-level iPad and iPad Pro lineup. The latter received OLED screens in 2024, so the inclusion of that technology on the latest iPad mini now is noteworthy. Why are fans so keen on an OLED iPad mini? OLED displays offer better contrast and deeper blacks, resulting in higher-quality images overall. Flagship smartphones like the iPhone 18 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 use OLED screens too, so updating the iPad mini to have the same technology will make it look and feel more modern. But most popular smartphones also have 120Hz refresh rates, which makes scrolling feel quicker and smoother. Apple appears to have skipped this on the new iPad mini (no refresh rate is listed in the new iPad mini's specs; we've reached out to Apple to confirm) and that will likely be a deal breaker for some who find the standard 60Hz to feel too sluggish in comparison. There's also the argument that one could simply get an iPhone Duo now, which has similar dimensions to the iPad mini when unfolded, along with an OLED screen and a 120Hz refresh rate. But the iPhone Duo costs $2,000, and it seems to be having some unique issues of its own at the moment, just days after its official launch. The new iPad mini's A20 Pro processor should give it a decent performance boost, while the 12MP Center Stage camera on its landscape edge should make it more convenient to make FaceTime video calls. The nano-texture display option appears similar to that of the iPhone Duo's inner display, which is designed to reduce glare. Note, though, that this feature is optional on the iPad mini, is only available on the 256GB and 512GB storage options and bumps up the final price by an additional $100. Pre-orders open for the new iPad mini on Oct. 28, and it will be widely available starting Nov. 6.

The display experience on the new mini should be much more in line with what we’ve come to expect from Apple’s Pro-level devices. The 2-nanometer A20 Pro chip was a noticeable upgrade in the iPhone 18 Pro , and it will be even more significant in this tablet. The previous model had a 3-nanometer A17 Pro chip, which was already a year old when it appeared in the iPad mini. In the iPhone 18 Pro, we found the A20 Pro significantly improved graphics performance thanks in part to a 50 percent increase in memory bandwidth. Higher memory speed also helps with on-device AI applications, but the Neural Engine is the primary factor. Unfortunately, not all versions of the new iPad mini will be equally capable. Apple notes the 512GB configuration will have the dual 16-core Neural Engine we saw in the iPhone 18 Pro, but the 128GB and 256GB versions will have a single 16-core NPU. These versions will also have a slightly different CPU configuration, with five cores instead of six. Apple has retained the 12 MP cameras for the front and back of the tablet, but the front-facing one has changed location. Rather than being on the short edge for portrait-orientation video calls, it’s now on the long edge. That might take a little getting used to for those who frequently use their tablets for FaceTime. The $699 base price gets you 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi connectivity. It’s $100 more for 256GB and $300 more for 512GB. The nano-texture display is also a $100 upsell, but it’s only available for the 256GB and 512GB versions. The step up to cellular will cost $849 for the 128GB model. Pricing is, sadly, not eye-popping for 2026, but it marks yet another price increase for Apple. The 7th-gen iPad mini launched for $499 in 2024, but it has since risen to $599. The new model adds $100, but it does have some nice upgrades. Preorders for the new iPad mini begin at 10:10 am PT on October 28 (Wednesday), and devices will arrive on doorsteps and in stores on November 6. extraction.body: Just as rumors last week suggested, the redesigned 8th-generation iPad Mini (2026) has arrived ahead of Apple's "Pro and Tell" event on Wednesday, October 28th. The refreshed pint-sized tablet features a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, an improved front-facing camera, and, for the first time on any iPad, IP67 water and dust resistance. The redesigned pint-sized tablet also features a less thick 5.4mm design and 24% thinner bezels. On the display front, the new 8.5-inch OLED screen offers 2x higher peak brightness at 1,200 nits (along with 1 nit minimum brightness), plus a nano-texture display option similar to recent iPad Pro releases. However, the new iPad Mini still doesn't feature a 120Hz ProMotion display and is locked to 60Hz. The 2024-released 7th-generation iPad Mini featured an 8.3-inch LCD screen with relatively thick bezels. The larger OLED panel should deliver deeper blacks, improved contrast, and more vibrant colors. At the same time, the tablet might also have worse battery life, since OLED panel technology consumes more power, though efficiency improvements in the A20 Pro could offset that. In the press release, Apple says that the new iPad Mini can hit 10 hours of battery life while watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi. Regarding the A20 Pro specifically, the chip features a 5-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, making it compatible with Apple's new Siri AI features, including the assistant's more expressive voice. It also has a 7-core GPU that delivers up to 2.7x faster graphics performance. Lastly, the 512GB model features a 6-core CPU. The tablet's front-facing camera has been upgraded to a 12-megapixel Center Stage shooter that sits on its landscape bezel edge. Other upgrades include the Acoustic Display, which Apple says features "specially designed woofers" that are "paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume." Lastly, the tablet features Apple's C2 cellular modem (if you opt for the cellular version), alongside its N1 wireless chip. Apple says the new iPad Mini will be available to pre-order on Wednesday, October 28th, starting at $700, with availability launching on November 6th. While the 8th-gen iPad Mini seems like a solid all-around upgrade thanks to the A20 Pro chip and the new OLED panel, it's a bit crazy that it starts at $700, especially since the last refresh in 2024 launched at $500 (which already felt pretty expensive). Later this week, Apple is expected to reveal a touch-screen MacBook Pro and the M6-powered MacBook Pro and iPad. New features include more accurate health tracking and longer battery life.

The 2024-released 7th-generation iPad Mini featured an 8.3-inch LCD screen with relatively thick bezels.

The larger OLED panel should deliver deeper blacks, improved contrast, and more vibrant colors. At the same time, the tablet might also have worse battery life, since OLED panel technology consumes more power, though efficiency improvements in the A20 Pro could offset that. In the press release, Apple says that the new iPad Mini can hit 10 hours of battery life while watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi.

Regarding the A20 Pro specifically, the chip features a 5-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, making it compatible with Apple's new Siri AI features, including the assistant's more expressive voice. It also has a 7-core GPU that delivers up to 2.7x faster graphics performance. Lastly, the 512GB model features a 6-core CPU.

While the 8th-gen iPad Mini seems like a solid all-around upgrade thanks to the A20 Pro chip and the new OLED panel, it's a bit crazy that it starts at $700, especially since the last refresh in 2024 launched at $500 (which already felt pretty expensive).
Later this week, Apple is expected to reveal a touch-screen MacBook Pro and the M6-powered MacBook Pro and iPad.
New features include more accurate health tracking and longer battery life.

sources.title: Apple’s new iPad mini finally gets an OLED screen — and a $100 price increase - Yahoo Tech
passages: Apple has been slow to update the iPad mini over the years, much to the chagrin of its niche yet vocal fanbase .
The previous generation came out in 2024, adding more storage, Apple Pencil support and a processor upgrade.
Apple has spent more time updating other iPad models, including the entry-level iPad and iPad Pro lineup.
The latter received OLED screens in 2024, so the inclusion of that technology on the latest iPad mini now is noteworthy.
Leading up to its "pro and tell" event later this week, Apple kicked off its latest round of announcements by revealing the new iPad mini .
The 8th-generation small tablet now comes with an 8.5-inch OLED display, a longstanding wish list item for many mini fans.
The new tablet also gains an updated A20 Pro processor, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a nano-texture option for the display.
It starts at $699, $100 more than the previous version, and will be available for pre-order on Oct.
But the iPhone Duo costs $2,000, and it seems to be having some unique issues of its own at the moment, just days after its official launch.
OLED displays offer better contrast and deeper blacks, resulting in higher-quality images overall.
But most popular smartphones also have 120Hz refresh rates, which makes scrolling feel quicker and smoother.

Leading up to its "pro and tell" event later this week, Apple kicked off its latest round of announcements by revealing the new iPad mini . The 8th-generation small tablet now comes with an 8.5-inch OLED display, a longstanding wish list item for many mini fans. The new tablet also gains an updated A20 Pro processor, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a nano-texture option for the display. It starts at $699, $100 more than the previous version, and will be available for pre-order on Oct. 28. Apple has been slow to update the iPad mini over the years, much to the chagrin of its niche yet vocal fanbase . The previous generation came out in 2024, adding more storage, Apple Pencil support and a processor upgrade. The version before that came out in 2021 and finally removed the aging Home button from the tiny tablet. Apple has spent more time updating other iPad models, including the entry-level iPad and iPad Pro lineup. The latter received OLED screens in 2024, so the inclusion of that technology on the latest iPad mini now is noteworthy. Why are fans so keen on an OLED iPad mini? OLED displays offer better contrast and deeper blacks, resulting in higher-quality images overall. Flagship smartphones like the iPhone 18 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 use OLED screens too, so updating the iPad mini to have the same technology will make it look and feel more modern. But most popular smartphones also have 120Hz refresh rates, which makes scrolling feel quicker and smoother. Apple appears to have skipped this on the new iPad mini (no refresh rate is listed in the new iPad mini's specs; we've reached out to Apple to confirm) and that will likely be a deal breaker for some who find the standard 60Hz to feel too sluggish in comparison. There's also the argument that one could simply get an iPhone Duo now, which has similar dimensions to the iPad mini when unfolded, along with an OLED screen and a 120Hz refresh rate. But the iPhone Duo costs $2,000, and it seems to be having some unique issues of its own at the moment, just days after its official launch. The new iPad mini's A20 Pro processor should give it a decent performance boost, while the 12MP Center Stage camera on its landscape edge should make it more convenient to make FaceTime video calls. The nano-texture display option appears similar to that of the iPhone Duo's inner display, which is designed to reduce glare. Note, though, that this feature is optional on the iPad mini, is only available on the 256GB and 512GB storage options and bumps up the final price by an additional $100. Pre-orders open for the new iPad mini on Oct. 28, and it will be widely available starting Nov. 6.

sources.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
passages: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models.

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers.
The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how.
For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.
He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers.
