extraction.body: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done. Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding. He recalled celebrating when his wife started leaving her computer on all night so that her agents could keep working. “On the product team, what I think about is, how do we make this intuitive and useful to people?” he told Disrupt attendees. “A lot of that isn’t building some new piece of tech into the product; it’s how you frame it to the user and how it feels.” Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers. Even the name—a play on the negative space inside of OpenAI’s logo—is intended “to feel like just something that could eventually be ubiquitous.” (Asked when he learned that rival AI entrepreneur Elon Musk owns the dot.com URL, Embiricos said, “I found out very late.”) The idea of a persistent agent is that it doesn’t need prompting. For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it. In our testing, the assistant’s ability to think ahead is apparent and often useful, but it isn’t quite there yet. It will flag calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines, but not necessarily in the most timely fashion. “The first time it told me about one of those [conflicts]—this is like early in development—it told me three minutes before the thing,” Embiricos says of his dot. “It’s like, ‘Hey, this thing is coming up. You might want to do something about it.’ I only have three minutes!” Embiricos expects the timing to improve over time, but the proactive approach is key to the product. “I was hearing about an engineer at a drone delivery startup, and they were saying, ‘We had this outage, and by the time I noticed that the outage was going on, my dot had already noticed the outage was happening, had already analyzed the outage, and had come to me with useful information for how we could resolve the outage.’” As with most AI agent use cases, there’s a tension between the personal information an AI model needs to be useful and exactly how much personal data you are exposing to a software company. Muse has been criticized for the profiles it builds of your family and friends, which the software uses to know, say, what kind of restaurant you might want to go to with a specific pal, but could also add incredible value to Meta’s advertising business. Does dots collect similar data? “Yes, we have a thing that we built into dots, which we call proactive research,” Embiricos said. “On a cadence, it will think about what it knows about you, what is the conversation that it’s had, and then what have you given it access to that it can think about, and then it will go and research, ‘What could I do to be more helpful to you?’ And then, basically, it will propose that.” It’s difficult to separate the data needs of the agent from that of its parent corporation. Hark, a start-up developing its own AI personal assistant, is explicit in pointing out it that it doesn’t collect data to fuel an advertising business the way that OpenAI and Meta do. With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how. Still, those controls aren’t granular and the app can be pushy. For example, it refuses to accept read-only access to cloud drives. “What I think we need to do is basically build out super, super, super granular controls,” Embiricos said, but he pointed to the model’s intelligence and discretion as the other side of this coin. “This is actually something we kind of got some flack about when we launched,” Embiricos said. “We had really conservative defaults over what the agent would do, and it would ask for permission a lot. I remember knowing that we were going to see that feedback, but thinking, ‘This is okay, we can tune that over time.’” The other big question about AI agents is whether they can scale. They’re fun when only a few people have them, and stories of agents snagging hard-to-get reservations abound. But businesses don’t necessarily like dealing with agents and might not be equipped to. People certainly don’t like dealing with them (note: stop having your AI agents pitch me), and Embiricos is among those people. He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.” If the AI industry is right that agents are our future, can we get there without overwhelming the infrastructure that our world currently runs on, from businesses and websites to payment networks? “At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem. I probably can’t say too much here, but we’re deep in lots of conversations with payment processors.” Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers. Giving an assistant access to my email inbox already feels like a big ask, but my bank account is off limits. For now.

sources.title: OpenAI Unveils Always-On AI Agent Dots to Chase Meta's Muse
passages: SILICON VALLEY/BEIJING — OpenAI unveiled Dots, an artificial intelligence agent that runs around the clock, setting up a fierce rivalry with Meta's Muse.
OpenAI countered with its coding tool Codex, only to face another challenge on the 8th of this month when Meta introduced Muse, a free personal agent.
Chinese companies, spurred by Muse's popularity, are rolling out agents of their own, extending the U.S.-China AI contest from large language models into the market for agents.
Muse, backed by social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that draw more than 3 billion active users a day, overtook ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app.
Meta also expanded Muse to small and mid-sized businesses on the same day, signaling that it is targeting corporate customers as well as individual users.
OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman introduced Dots on the 29th at DevDay 2026, the company's annual developer conference, held at the Fort Mason Center in San Francisco.
Dots runs on GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most advanced model, giving it strong performance.
OpenAI engineers are using Dots to fix dozens of software bugs a day.
The arrival of Dots is expected to intensify competition among agents.
OpenAI led the chatbot market after launching ChatGPT in November 2022, but lost the initiative early this year when rival Anthropic released enterprise AI and coding tools.
OpenAI will offer Dots first to users of its enterprise products and subscribers to ChatGPT Pro, its higher-tier plan, and plans to widen access over time.
Alibaba has been expanding its AI chatbot Qwen since November last year into a personal assistant that performs real tasks by linking to shopping, travel and mobile payment services.

extraction.body: OpenAI launched Dots on September 29, turning ChatGPT into an always-on agent that can keep working after a conversation ends. The OpenAI Dots agent has a friendly avatar, a customizable name, and enough access to order dinner. Yet its design, permissions, and strongest early results point firmly toward workplace software. That tension matters because consumer agents usually compete on convenience. Meta’s Muse and similar products promise a personal shopper, travel planner, and universal checkout assistant. OpenAI instead gives its agent a cloud computer, connected applications, optional local computer access, and controls that resemble an IT administration console. The difference becomes clear when Dots meets the open web. It can search email, prepare a purchase, or navigate a service, but security checks often force the user back into control. Give it a website, media files, or another environment you manage, and the product starts looking much more capable. OpenAI is therefore testing a larger proposition than automated dinner orders. It wants people and companies to delegate ongoing responsibilities to software that can remember context, operate applications, and return completed work. The cute character is the invitation. The real product is an autonomous coworker. Dots changes ChatGPT from a destination for questions into a worker that can retain responsibility for an unfinished goal. OpenAI introduced Dots during DevDay 2026 in San Francisco. The company describes a dot as an always-on agent powered by GPT-6 Astra. An agent is software that can plan and perform several actions toward a goal, rather than only generating a response. Each dot receives its own cloud computer. It can use websites, run applications, consult connected services, and continue making progress between conversations. Users can inspect its activity, redirect it, or stop it while work is underway. Its interface presents the dot as a personable character. Users choose a name and interact through chat or voice. A separate view exposes the cloud computer, letting the owner watch the agent navigate software and websites. That visual approach resembles Meta Muse, but the underlying framing differs. Muse presents the agent as an approachable personal helper. Dots looks more like a managed workstation operated by an AI employee. The distinction appears in OpenAI’s enterprise controls. Workspace administrators can enable or disable Dots, connected applications, cloud browsing, network access, and local computer control. They can also decide whether members may add their agents to workplace messaging systems. Enterprise access starts disabled by default. Local computer access and customizable action rules also require separate permission. According to OpenAI’s workspace controls , enabling the agent does not automatically grant every connected service or computer capability. Those settings reveal OpenAI’s intended destination. Ordering food makes an accessible demonstration, but administering autonomous software requires identity, permission, auditability, and policy. Those are enterprise requirements. The persistence also changes how users must formulate requests. A dot works best with a responsibility, relevant context, and clear boundaries. “Keep this project moving” fits the design better than a disconnected sequence of small prompts. This is close to an AI workflow , where information, decisions, and repeated actions remain connected over time. The agent becomes valuable when it can carry context across those steps. That is the first reversal behind Dots. OpenAI wrapped a serious delegation system in a charming character. The personality makes the software approachable, but its operational model belongs in the workplace. The most important contrast is not OpenAI against Meta as companies. It is managed delegation against consumer convenience. Consumer agents sell a simple idea. Ask for an outcome, watch the software cross several websites, and approve the final transaction. Shopping, reservations, travel planning, and personal scheduling are natural demonstrations because everyone understands the friction. OpenAI can support those scenarios. In one company demonstration, a dot noticed that its user would work through dinner. It then prepared two delivery choices, including estimated costs, and asked which meal should be ordered. That demonstration made the agent feel personal and proactive. However, OpenAI devoted substantial product architecture to responsibilities that extend far beyond a meal. Dots can use workplace applications, retain project context, access a local machine, and eventually divide work among multiple agents. The company has also discussed specialist dots for enterprise customers. These agents would focus on defined areas such as accounting, marketing, or legal analysis. A specialist structure assumes organizations will assign responsibilities, evaluate outputs, and govern access by role. Ordering dinner has a lower ceiling. Saving several minutes is useful, but a security challenge or failed login can erase the benefit. A person who must repeatedly rescue an agent may return to the ordinary app. The consumer and enterprise routes also face different business pressures. A mass-market assistant must reach many users and find a sustainable commercial model. A workplace agent can justify itself through completed projects, reduced delays, or expanded capacity. Neither route guarantees reliable performance. Enterprise environments contain sensitive information and consequential actions. Their structured software may help an agent operate, but mistakes can carry greater costs. OpenAI appears to be betting that governance can make broader access acceptable. Administrators can restrict capabilities, while users can define custom rules for supported actions. Sensitive steps can trigger approval or require the person to take over. The cute avatar softens that administrative reality. It encourages conversation and makes delegation feel less like configuring an automation server. However, the agent’s usefulness still depends on careful setup. Dots therefore pressures both sides of the market. Consumer agents must show that convenience remains valuable when websites resist automation. Enterprise platforms must make controls usable without turning every task into a compliance project. OpenAI’s strongest advantage may be the connection between those worlds. The same agent can receive a casual voice instruction, search business context, operate software, and send progress updates to a phone. That continuity is more significant than the avatar. Disconnecting an external service stops new access. It does not automatically remove information already incorporated into the dot’s context. That behavior deserves attention before users connect broad archives. Data treatment also varies by account type and settings. OpenAI says it does not use Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspace data for model training by default. Personal accounts rely on the user’s model-improvement setting. The company’s privacy guidance says limited human review can still occur in safety-related circumstances. Users should read those controls before placing confidential material inside an agent’s working context. This creates a contest over the primary work interface. If users begin a project with their dot, individual applications can become resources in the background. If platform vendors keep agents inside their suites, ChatGPT remains one tool among many. OpenAI is preparing for both possibilities. Dots can communicate through Slack and Microsoft Teams, while enterprise administrators retain controls over access. The company has also discussed integration with Microsoft’s agent management systems. The long-term vision includes teams of dots. That idea raises the stakes because organizations would manage portfolios of agents, not one assistant. Agents could specialize, exchange work, and escalate decisions to people. Evidence of growing agent use also supports the timing. OpenAI reported that agentic activity represented 64 percent of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers by June 2026. The company defines that measure using Codex activity, so it should not be read as independent market data. Still, the figure shows why OpenAI is expanding the Codex pattern. Coding agents demonstrated that users will delegate multistep work when outputs can be inspected and corrected. Dots attempts to apply that pattern beyond software development. The Verge’s description of Dots as “Codex, but for regular people” captures the strategy. Code offers structured files, tools, tests, and version control. General knowledge work lacks many of those safeguards.

Dots therefore pressures both sides of the market. Consumer agents must show that convenience remains valuable when websites resist automation. Enterprise platforms must make controls usable without turning every task into a compliance project.

OpenAI’s strongest advantage may be the connection between those worlds. The same agent can receive a casual voice instruction, search business context, operate software, and send progress updates to a phone. That continuity is more significant than the avatar.

Disconnecting an external service stops new access. It does not automatically remove information already incorporated into the dot’s context. That behavior deserves attention before users connect broad archives.

Data treatment also varies by account type and settings. OpenAI says it does not use Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspace data for model training by default. Personal accounts rely on the user’s model-improvement setting.

The company’s privacy guidance says limited human review can still occur in safety-related circumstances. Users should read those controls before placing confidential material inside an agent’s working context.

This creates a contest over the primary work interface. If users begin a project with their dot, individual applications can become resources in the background. If platform vendors keep agents inside their suites, ChatGPT remains one tool among many.

OpenAI is preparing for both possibilities. Dots can communicate through Slack and Microsoft Teams, while enterprise administrators retain controls over access. The company has also discussed integration with Microsoft’s agent management systems.

The long-term vision includes teams of dots. That idea raises the stakes because organizations would manage portfolios of agents, not one assistant. Agents could specialize, exchange work, and escalate decisions to people.

Evidence of growing agent use also supports the timing. OpenAI reported that agentic activity represented 64 percent of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers by June 2026. The company defines that measure using Codex activity, so it should not be read as independent market data.

Still, the figure shows why OpenAI is expanding the Codex pattern. Coding agents demonstrated that users will delegate multistep work when outputs can be inspected and corrected. Dots attempts to apply that pattern beyond software development.

The Verge’s description of Dots as “Codex, but for regular people” captures the strategy. Code offers structured files, tools, tests, and version control. General knowledge work lacks many of those safeguards.

coreStoryFacts.text: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models.

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers.
The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how.
For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.
He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers.
OpenAI used its Dev Day event on Tuesday to unveil Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra.
The company describes the agents as capable, always-on systems built to handle tasks continuously with minimal supervision.
It was stated that OpenAI is currently collaborating with Microsoft to incorporate Dots within Agent 365, which is Microsoft's framework for enterprise AI agents.

OpenAI also confirmed users will be able to message their Dots through workplace platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams, with text message support planned for a future update.
Specialist Dots, where each dot is assigned an identity, credentials, and certain tools according to its function, is another thing that OpenAI brings forward.

extraction.body: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it. Muse has been criticized for the profiles it builds of your family and friends, which the software uses to know, say, what kind of restaurant you might want to go to with a specific pal, but could also add incredible value to Meta’s advertising business. Hark, a start-up developing its own AI personal assistant, is explicit in pointing out it that it doesn’t collect data to fuel an advertising business the way that OpenAI and Meta do. With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how. Still, those controls aren’t granular and the app can be pushy. For example, it refuses to accept read-only access to cloud drives. “What I think we need to do is basically build out super, super, super granular controls,” Embiricos said, but he pointed to the model’s intelligence and discretion as the other side of this coin. “This is actually something we kind of got some flack about when we launched,” Embiricos said. “We had really conservative defaults over what the agent would do, and it would ask for permission a lot. I remember knowing that we were going to see that feedback, but thinking, ‘This is okay, we can tune that over time.’” The other big question about AI agents is whether they can scale. People certainly don’t like dealing with them (note: stop having your AI agents pitch me), and Embiricos is among those people. He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.” If the AI industry is right that agents are our future, can we get there without overwhelming the infrastructure that our world currently runs on, from businesses and websites to payment networks? “At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem. sources.title: OpenAI launches dots, an always-on agentic assistant - The News International
passages: OpenAI used its Dev Day event on Tuesday to unveil Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra.
The company describes the agents as capable, always-on systems built to handle tasks continuously with minimal supervision.
It was stated that OpenAI is currently collaborating with Microsoft to incorporate Dots within Agent 365, which is Microsoft's framework for enterprise AI agents.

OpenAI framed the launch as an evolving system, describing plans for users to eventually deploy multiple Dots working together on their behalf, starting with a single primary Dot that can be named and customised.
OpenAI also confirmed users will be able to message their Dots through workplace platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams, with text message support planned for a future update.
Specialist Dots, where each dot is assigned an identity, credentials, and certain tools according to its function, is another thing that OpenAI brings forward.

sources.title: OpenAI Unveils Always-On AI Agent Dots to Chase Meta's Muse
passages: SILICON VALLEY/BEIJING — OpenAI unveiled Dots, an artificial intelligence agent that runs around the clock, setting up a fierce rivalry with Meta's Muse.
OpenAI countered with its coding tool Codex, only to face another challenge on the 8th of this month when Meta introduced Muse, a free personal agent.
Chinese companies, spurred by Muse's popularity, are rolling out agents of their own, extending the U.S.-China AI contest from large language models into the market for agents.
Muse, backed by social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that draw more than 3 billion active users a day, overtook ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app.
Meta also expanded Muse to small and mid-sized businesses on the same day, signaling that it is targeting corporate customers as well as individual users.
OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman introduced Dots on the 29th at DevDay 2026, the company's annual developer conference, held at the Fort Mason Center in San Francisco.
Dots runs on GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most advanced model, giving it strong performance.
OpenAI engineers are using Dots to fix dozens of software bugs a day.
The arrival of Dots is expected to intensify competition among agents.
OpenAI led the chatbot market after launching ChatGPT in November 2022, but lost the initiative early this year when rival Anthropic released enterprise AI and coding tools.
OpenAI will offer Dots first to users of its enterprise products and subscribers to ChatGPT Pro, its higher-tier plan, and plans to widen access over time.
Alibaba has been expanding its AI chatbot Qwen since November last year into a personal assistant that performs real tasks by linking to shopping, travel and mobile payment services.

passages: Apple on Monday announced a new iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display.
The tablet features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor and is powered by an A20 Pro chip.
The tech giant revealed the new device just days before its “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday.
Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, the iPad mini has up to 4.5-times faster AI performance than the previous generation, according to Apple.
It also features an “Acoustic Display” that Apple says enhances the audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content.
Specially designed woofers integrated into the display deliver deeper bass and higher volume for richer sound, per the company.
The Super Retina XDR display uses OLED technology for pixel-level lighting control, delivering deeper blacks, richer contrast, and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vibrant colors.

extraction.body: For small businesses that need a full-featured computer without adding another bulky laptop to the travel bag, Apple is positioning its redesigned iPad mini as a mobile work tool rather than simply a compact tablet. Apple announced the new iPad mini on October 26, saying the device delivers its largest update yet. The company highlighted an 8.5-inch OLED display, a thinner and lighter design, the A20 Pro processor, faster wireless connectivity, water and dust resistance, and new artificial intelligence capabilities through iPadOS 27. Customers can pre-order the device beginning October 28, with shipments and retail availability starting November 6. Prices start at $699 for the Wi-Fi model and $849 for the Wi-Fi + Cellular version in the United States. Apple says the new model measures 5.4 millimeters thick and weighs less than its predecessor. Its IP67 rating means it can withstand dust and immersion in up to one meter of water for as long as 30 minutes under controlled laboratory conditions. That could benefit contractors checking plans outdoors, restaurant managers moving between locations, or shop owners using a tablet near sinks and work counters. However, the rating does not make the iPad mini waterproof for everyday business purposes. Apple warns that resistance can decline with normal wear and that users should not charge a wet device. Liquid damage is not covered under warranty, an important consideration for companies working in unpredictable environments. The display represents one of the more visible upgrades. Apple says the OLED panel produces deeper blacks, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. A new nano-texture option reduces glare in bright surroundings. For a photographer, designer, architect, or field technician, that could make reviewing images, diagrams, and documents easier outdoors. The nano-texture version may carry additional cost, however, and business owners should confirm pricing before budgeting for multiple employees. Performance could matter more for businesses using demanding applications. Apple claims the A20 Pro can accelerate on-device AI, local language models, photo editing, graphics work, and 3D rendering. The 512GB configuration includes a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says doubles the processing power of the previous generation for certain AI workloads. Those claims come from Apple’s own testing, conducted in September 2026. Actual performance will depend on the software, workload, storage configuration, and whether an application processes data on the device or through the cloud. Businesses should test their core applications before replacing existing laptops or tablets across a team. The iPad mini also adds a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera positioned on the landscape edge. That arrangement could improve video calls when the tablet sits in a stand or connects to a keyboard. The rear camera supports 4K video and an Adaptive True Tone flash, which may help employees scan documents, capture inventory, record job progress, or create social media content. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.” Connectivity could make the cellular version attractive to mobile businesses. Apple says its C2 modem supports up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds than the prior model, while the N1 wireless chip enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular connectivity could help salespeople, inspectors, delivery operators, and service technicians stay connected away from office networks. It also adds a recurring data-plan expense, and speeds will vary by carrier, location, and network conditions. Apple’s most consequential software pitch involves artificial intelligence. Siri AI, which rolls out in beta with iPadOS 27, can use personal context, interpret onscreen information, and answer questions. Apple Intelligence also includes upgraded photo tools, Image Playground, systemwide dictation improvements, and Safari notifications for changes such as product restocks or price drops. For small businesses, those tools could reduce time spent searching through messages, rewriting notes, editing images, and monitoring web pages. Privacy may appeal to companies handling sensitive information: Apple says many requests use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, and that data handled through Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple. Still, AI should not be treated as a substitute for review. Siri AI remains in beta, some features are unavailable in certain regions or languages, and Apple says server-based tools may face daily usage limits. Owners should also establish policies for confidential customer, employee, and financial information before allowing staff to use AI features. The tablet supports Apple Pencil USB-C for $79 and Apple Pencil Pro for $129, while the new Smart Folio costs $79. Those extras can quickly raise the total cost of ownership. A Wi-Fi model with the Pencil Pro and folio reaches $907 before taxes, and a cellular model with the same accessories reaches $1,057. Apple offers trade-in credits, installment plans, leasing, and AppleCare options. Financing can reduce the immediate cash burden, but eligibility requirements, credit approval, carrier conditions, and lease termination charges apply. Businesses should compare the full cost with a laptop, an existing tablet, or a refurbished device before committing. The new iPad mini is available in midnight and starlight finishes with 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB storage. More details are available in Apple’s original announcement . For owners who value portability and already use Apple software, the device could become a flexible tool for communication, field operations, content creation, and light productivity. For teams that rely on desktop software, extensive typing, or large screens, it may work best as a targeted mobile companion rather than a universal computer replacement. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”

Connectivity could make the cellular version attractive to mobile businesses. Apple says its C2 modem supports up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds than the prior model, while the N1 wireless chip enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular connectivity could help salespeople, inspectors, delivery operators, and service technicians stay connected away from office networks. It also adds a recurring data-plan expense, and speeds will vary by carrier, location, and network conditions.

Apple’s most consequential software pitch involves artificial intelligence. Siri AI, which rolls out in beta with iPadOS 27, can use personal context, interpret onscreen information, and answer questions. Apple Intelligence also includes upgraded photo tools, Image Playground, systemwide dictation improvements, and Safari notifications for changes such as product restocks or price drops.

For small businesses, those tools could reduce time spent searching through messages, rewriting notes, editing images, and monitoring web pages. Privacy may appeal to companies handling sensitive information: Apple says many requests use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, and that data handled through Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple.

Still, AI should not be treated as a substitute for review. Siri AI remains in beta, some features are unavailable in certain regions or languages, and Apple says server-based tools may face daily usage limits. Owners should also establish policies for confidential customer, employee, and financial information before allowing staff to use AI features.

The tablet supports Apple Pencil USB-C for $79 and Apple Pencil Pro for $129, while the new Smart Folio costs $79. Those extras can quickly raise the total cost of ownership. A Wi-Fi model with the Pencil Pro and folio reaches $907 before taxes, and a cellular model with the same accessories reaches $1,057.

Apple offers trade-in credits, installment plans, leasing, and AppleCare options. Financing can reduce the immediate cash burden, but eligibility requirements, credit approval, carrier conditions, and lease termination charges apply. Businesses should compare the full cost with a laptop, an existing tablet, or a refurbished device before committing.

The new iPad mini is available in midnight and starlight finishes with 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB storage. More details are available in Apple’s original announcement . For owners who value portability and already use Apple software, the device could become a flexible tool for communication, field operations, content creation, and light productivity. For teams that rely on desktop software, extensive typing, or large screens, it may work best as a targeted mobile companion rather than a universal computer replacement.

Apple announced the new iPad mini on October 26, saying the device delivers its largest update yet. Customers can pre-order the device beginning October 28, with shipments and retail availability starting November 6. Prices start at $699 for the Wi-Fi model and $849 for the Wi-Fi + Cellular version in the United States. Apple says the new model measures 5.4 millimeters thick and weighs less than its predecessor. Its IP67 rating means it can withstand dust and immersion in up to one meter of water for as long as 30 minutes under controlled laboratory conditions. That could benefit contractors checking plans outdoors, restaurant managers moving between locations, or shop owners using a tablet near sinks and work counters. However, the rating does not make the iPad mini waterproof for everyday business purposes. Apple warns that resistance can decline with normal wear and that users should not charge a wet device. Liquid damage is not covered under warranty, an important consideration for companies working in unpredictable environments. The display represents one of the more visible upgrades. Apple says the OLED panel produces deeper blacks, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. A new nano-texture option reduces glare in bright surroundings. For a photographer, designer, architect, or field technician, that could make reviewing images, diagrams, and documents easier outdoors. The 512GB configuration includes a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says doubles the processing power of the previous generation for certain AI workloads. Those claims come from Apple’s own testing, conducted in September 2026. passages: If you had invested $1,000 in Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), XRP (CRYPTO:XRP), or Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) five years ago, you bought in close to the peak of a major market rally.
Bitcoin closed October 2021 at $61,340 and hit a high of $68,770 in November 2021, shortly before the market began to decline.
As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Bitcoin emerged as the top performer, yielding a 36.6% gain over five years, while XRP followed closely with a 29.5% increase.
In contrast, Ethereum and Solana are still trading significantly below their prices from October 2021.
To break even, Ethereum would need to surpass $3,954, an increase of about 70%, and Solana would need to rise above $185, about 83% higher.
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.
Even Ethereum and XRP investors faced significant losses after experiencing gains.
Unfortunately, both coins saw declines of 51.0% for XRP and 44.0% for Ethereum in the following year.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%.
However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
Bitcoin may maintain its leading position as it has gained the most of these coins since 2021.
If Bitcoin stays above $79,107 (its low in October 2026), the initial $1,000 investment keeps showing a solid profit.
However, if it falls below $58,681, that gain could disappear entirely.

Of the four cryptocurrencies, two gained value while two lost almost half their value.

passages: Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%. However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
We examined a $1,000 investment in each coin made on October 27, 2021, and evaluated their worth recently. Of the four cryptocurrencies, two gained value while two lost almost half their value.

On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.

Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.

Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

story.title: What If You Had Put $1,000 Into Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana 5 Years Ago? - 24/7 Wall St.

facts.text: If you had invested $1,000 in Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), XRP (CRYPTO:XRP), or Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) five years ago, you bought in close to the peak of a major market rally.
Bitcoin closed October 2021 at $61,340 and hit a high of $68,770 in November 2021, shortly before the market began to decline.
As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Bitcoin emerged as the top performer, yielding a 36.6% gain over five years, while XRP followed closely with a 29.5% increase.
In contrast, Ethereum and Solana are still trading significantly below their prices from October 2021.
To break even, Ethereum would need to surpass $3,954, an increase of about 70%, and Solana would need to rise above $185, about 83% higher.
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.
Even Ethereum and XRP investors faced significant losses after experiencing gains.
Unfortunately, both coins saw declines of 51.0% for XRP and 44.0% for Ethereum in the following year.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%.
However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
Bitcoin may maintain its leading position as it has gained the most of these coins since 2021.
If Bitcoin stays above $79,107 (its low in October 2026), the initial $1,000 investment keeps showing a solid profit.
However, if it falls below $58,681, that gain could disappear entirely.

Its lowest monthly price during this period was $348 in October 2022, a 24% dip—much less severe than Bitcoin's or Solana's drops.
It then surged to its all-time high in October 2025, making that stake worth around $2,150.
It plummeted to a low of $8.12 in December 2022, cutting the initial investment down to about $44, a staggering 95.6% loss.
However, it rebounded to $295 in January 2025, bringing that stake back up to about $1,597.

Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

sources.title: If You Put $1,000 Each Into Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana Five Years Ago, Two Would Have Lost Money. - AOL.com
passages: Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

passages: A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown.
The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.
A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server.

In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.
The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21.
Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin.
PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes.
Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.
The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell.
A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process.
That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier. The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours. The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server. The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote. PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account. The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt. The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code. Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet. Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password. The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024. A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who r ecovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin. The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all. A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.

The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours.

The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.

The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote.

PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.

The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt.

The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code.

Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet.

Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.

The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024.

A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who r ecovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin.

The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

story.title: Bitcoin reward offered to anyone who could break into an unpatched server running PHP, hacker cracks site and claims bounty — PHP2Shell challenge tested claims that AI makes exploiting vulnerabilities easy - Tom's Hardware

facts.text: A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown.
The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.
A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server.

In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.
The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21.
Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin.
PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes.
Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.
The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell.
A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process.
That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier. The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours. The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server. The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote. PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account. The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt. The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code. Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet. Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password. The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024. A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who r ecovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin. The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all. A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.

The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours.

The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.

The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote.

PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.

The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt.

The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code.

Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet.

Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.

The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024.

A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who r ecovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin.

The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.
