extraction.body: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever Featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance, faster wireless connectivity, and water and dust resistance CUPERTINO, CALIFORNIA Apple today unveiled the all-new iPad mini , featuring a stunning OLED display in an even thinner and lighter design, a huge leap in performance with A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance. 1 The larger 8.5-inch OLED display, also available with a nano-texture option, delivers higher contrast and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini for a brilliant and immersive viewing experience. 2 A20 Pro supercharges AI with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core and Dual 16-core Neural Engine. iPad mini now has a 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge that’s perfect for video calls, an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience, faster wireless and cellular connectivity, and fast-charge support. 3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever. The new iPad mini is powered by iPadOS 27 with the next generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI, which can draw on a user’s personal context to help them find what they need, answer questions on virtually any topic with broad world knowledge, and understand what’s on their screen. 4 The combination of powerful features and game-changing iPadOS 27 capabilities makes the new iPad mini a compelling value. Customers can pre-order it along with the new Smart Folio starting Wednesday, October 28, with availability beginning Friday, November 6. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.” At 5.4 mm thin, the new iPad mini is more portable than ever, and is available in two gorgeous finishes: a new midnight and a beautiful starlight. Remarkably thinner and lighter than the previous generation, iPad mini is now even easier to carry, whether a user is reading, working on the go, or using it with one hand. It also features an IP67 rating to protect against water and dust — ideal for a range of use cases, such as working outside on a rainy day or reading by the pool. 1 The new iPad mini comes with a stunning OLED display that delivers amazing front-of-screen performance and an even larger 8.5-inch size while maintaining the same footprint as the previous mini, thanks to 24 percent thinner bezels. 2 The Super Retina XDR display features OLED technology to deliver pixel-level lighting control for much deeper blacks and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vivid and accurate imagery. For an even better visual experience across a range of lighting conditions, iPad mini also features peak brightness of up to 1200 nits — more than 2x higher than the previous generation — and supports 600 nits of full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content, along with a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio. And with a 1-nit minimum brightness, iPad mini is even more suitable for dim environments, from users reading in bed at night to pilots checking their electronic flight bag in the cockpit. iPad mini also offers a new nano-texture display option, which users love on iPad Pro, that reduces glare in bright environments — ideal for creatives editing outdoors or technicians working in the field. Together, these display advancements extend the versatility of iPad mini across an even wider range of use cases. A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks. It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips. Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each GPU core, iPad mini delivers up to 4.5x faster AI performance than the previous generation — perfect for AI tasks ranging from running on-device models in creative apps to running local LLMs. 3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering. 3 A20 Pro also features up to a 6-core CPU for up to 60 percent faster multithreaded performance for everyday tasks like editing photos and working across apps. 3 The 512GB configuration features a powerful Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which offers double the processing power of the previous generation, accelerating tasks in apps like Draw Things and Detail. By engaging all 32 cores, A20 Pro becomes a powerhouse for more advanced on-device AI workloads. A20 Pro also brings over a 2x increase in unified memory bandwidth, unlocking additional performance for new levels of capability and responsiveness across graphics and AI-intensive workloads. A Rich New Audio Experience and Advanced Cameras The new iPad mini features an innovative Acoustic Display for an even better audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content. Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume. In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs. The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating. The 12MP Center Stage front camera is now on the landscape edge, perfect for FaceTime calls, video conferencing, and collaboration. And the 12MP Wide back camera captures gorgeous photos with Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, while the addition of an Adaptive True Tone flash improves photos and makes document scanning better than ever. iPad mini now features N1, an Apple-designed wireless networking chip that enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. 5 N1 brings better performance when connected to 5GHz Wi-Fi networks and improves the overall performance and reliability of features like AirDrop and AirPlay. 6 Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system. C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency. 6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit. Users can also enjoy the benefits of eSIM, which lets them quickly and securely add a new plan, connect and transfer existing plans digitally, and stay in touch with family and friends regardless of Wi-Fi availability. 7 iPadOS 27 with the Next Generation of Apple Intelligence and Siri AI iPad mini users can get even more done with Siri AI, rolling out in beta with iPadOS 27. Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational. 4 iPad mini also supports Apple’s most advanced on-device model ever, for even more expressive voices with Siri AI as well as a major boost in accuracy with systemwide dictation. Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic. Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful. Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend. And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery. In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates. Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy. When Private Cloud Compute is handling users’ requests, their personal data is not stored nor made accessible to Apple or anyone else. iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference. With iPadOS 27.2, iPad mini also supports extended display mode when connected to an external display, great for users multitasking with windowed apps. Additionally, powerful and easy-to-use tools help parents manage what their kids can see, who they can talk to, and when they have access to apps. For parents and families looking for more information on how to help create safer, more enriching digital experiences for their kids, Apple also has a website with details on the latest tools and how to get started using them. Accessories That Unlock More Ways to Be Productive and Creative The new Smart Folio features a two-panel architecture, offering a slim, lightweight cover that magnetically attaches to iPad mini. 8 Crafted with TechWoven fabric in navy blue and taupe to complement the iPad mini finishes, the Smart Folio has an adjustable design that gives users a greater range of motion, including new viewing angles, for enhanced versatility. iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life. 8 Apple Pencil (USB-C) is a great value for everyday tasks like note-taking and sketching, while Apple Pencil Pro delivers industry-leading capabilities for the ultimate pencil experience. With Apple Pencil Pro, users can take advantage of innovative features like squeeze and barrel roll to work in entirely new ways, as well as utilize Find My support to help locate it when misplaced. iPad mini was built with the environment in mind and drives progress toward Apple’s ambitious plan to be carbon neutral across its entire footprint by 2030. It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain. It is designed to be durable and repairable, and meets Apple’s high standards for energy efficiency and safe chemistry. As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled. Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984. Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro. Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV. Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it. The latest news and updates, direct from Apple.

The larger 8.5-inch OLED display (up slightly from the 8.3-inch screen used previously) is available with a nano-texture option, delivering higher contrast, reduced glare, and more than 2x higher peak brightness than the previous-generation iPad mini. A new 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge makes the new camera even better for video calls, while the device's new Acoustic Display provides an improved better audio experience, while eliminating speaker holes. A nano-texture display option is also available.

Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies.
Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.

The new iPad mini also measures just 5.4mm thin, making it the most portable version of the device yet; on the processing side, the iPad mini now comes with the A20 Pro chip, carried straight from the iPhone 18 Pro – so you get all the latest and greatest Apple has to offer this year in a slightly bigger format. The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.

Despite housing a larger 8.5-inch screen, the overall footprint remains the same as the previous generation, thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner. The Super Retina XDR OLED display brings deeper blacks and supports the Apple P3 wide color gamut, with peak brightness reaching up to 1,200 nits (more than twice that of the previous generation, Apple says), while full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content sits at 600 nits. A nano-texture display option is also available.

Audio has also been reworked through an Acoustic Display system, similar to Sony’s BRAVIA TVs which uses the entire panel to improve audio quality. Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies. Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash. Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).

Pre-orders for the new iPad mini open on 29 October 2026 via apple.com/my and the Apple Store app; units will begin arriving to customers and appear in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorised Resellers from 6 November 2026. The tablet is available in 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB configurations in Midnight and Starlight finishes. The Wi-Fi model starts at RM2,999 , while the Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at RM3,699 .

Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.
The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.
A nano-texture display option is also available.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash.

Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).

Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies.
Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple says the A20 Pro chip offers up to 60% faster CPU performance, up to 2.7× faster graphics performance, and up to 4.5× faster AI performance compared to the A17 Pro chip that powered the previous iPad mini. A new 12MP Center Stage front camera on the landscape edge makes the new camera even better for video calls, while the device's new Acoustic Display provides an improved better audio experience, while eliminating speaker holes. Faster wireless and cellular connectivity come along for the ride in the form of Apple's N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. "Specially designed woofers are paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume," said Apple. "In addition, custom tweeters are now hidden between the glass and aluminum enclosure for clearer highs." Fast-charge support also makes an appearance. passages: Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.
The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.
A nano-texture display option is also available.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash.

Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).
Audio has also been reworked through an Acoustic Display system, similar to Sony’s BRAVIA TVs which uses the entire panel to improve audio quality.
Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies.
Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has unveiled the all-new iPad mini , and the company is calling it the biggest update the compact tablet has ever received – namely, it’s got a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the new A20 Pro chip, a thinner and lighter design, and an IP67 water and dust resistance rating.

The new iPad mini also measures just 5.4mm thin, making it the most portable version of the device yet; on the processing side, the iPad mini now comes with the A20 Pro chip, carried straight from the iPhone 18 Pro – so you get all the latest and greatest Apple has to offer this year in a slightly bigger format. The 512GB configuration also features a Dual 16-core Neural Engine with double the AI processing power of the previous generation.

Despite housing a larger 8.5-inch screen, the overall footprint remains the same as the previous generation, thanks to bezels that are 24% thinner. The Super Retina XDR OLED display brings deeper blacks and supports the Apple P3 wide color gamut, with peak brightness reaching up to 1,200 nits (more than twice that of the previous generation, Apple says), while full-screen brightness for SDR and HDR content sits at 600 nits. A nano-texture display option is also available.

Audio has also been reworked through an Acoustic Display system, similar to Sony’s BRAVIA TVs which uses the entire panel to improve audio quality. Woofers are paired through the display for punchier bass, while custom tweeters are tucked between the glass and aluminum enclosure for cleaner high frequencies. Since this design does away with speaker grilles, Apple claims this is one of the ways the tablet achieved its IP67 ingress protection rating.

Apple has also relocated the 12MP Center Stage front camera to the landscape edge for more natural video call framing, while the rear 12MP wide camera supports Smart HDR 4 and 4K video at up to 60 fps, alongside a new Adaptive True Tone flash. Connectivity receives a significant upgrade with the N1 wireless networking chip, enabling Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread support; cellular models gain the C2 modem, which Apple says delivers up to 50% faster cellular data speeds than before, with improved power efficiency (plus there’s eSIM support as well).

Pre-orders for the new iPad mini open on 29 October 2026 via apple.com/my and the Apple Store app; units will begin arriving to customers and appear in Apple Store locations and Apple Authorised Resellers from 6 November 2026. The tablet is available in 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB configurations in Midnight and Starlight finishes. The Wi-Fi model starts at RM2,999 , while the Wi-Fi + Cellular model starts at RM3,699 .

facts.text: Apple gives iPad mini its biggest update ever
Cellular models of the new iPad mini feature C2, Apple’s next-generation cellular modem system.
C2 enables up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds compared to the previous generation of iPad mini, with even greater power efficiency.
6 And with iPadOS 27, moving between cellular and Wi-Fi networks is more seamless than ever, so users can stay connected on a FaceTime call even while they’re in transit.
Siri AI is an entirely new version of Siri, powered by Apple Intelligence, that is profoundly more personal, capable, and conversational.
A20 Pro delivers a giant leap in performance for iPad mini, significantly boosting graphics and AI-intensive tasks.
It is built using Apple’s latest 2-nanometer process technology and a new package inspired by M-series chips.

3 And with the latest graphics architecture, including dynamic caching and hardware-accelerated mesh shading and ray tracing, graphics performance jumps by up to 2.7x — great for gaming and 3D rendering.

It is made with 35 percent recycled content overall, 9 including 100 percent recycled aluminum in the enclosure and 100 percent recycled cobalt in the battery. iPad mini is manufactured with 40 percent renewable energy, like wind and solar, across the supply chain.
As with all Apple products, its paper packaging is 100 percent fiber-based 10 and designed to be recycled.
3 With its incredible set of advanced features, it’s the most capable and versatile iPad mini ever.

iPadOS 27 also delivers an expansive set of improvements that make iPad more responsive, reliable, and easy to use, along with updates to Liquid Glass, including a new slider in Settings that gives users the option to personalize it, adjusting it anywhere from ultraclear to fully tinted to match their preference.
Apple revolutionized personal technology with the introduction of the Macintosh in 1984.
Today, Apple leads the world in innovation with iPhone, iPad, Mac, AirPods, Apple Watch, and Apple Vision Pro.

Apple’s six software platforms — iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, visionOS, and tvOS — provide seamless experiences across all Apple devices and empower people with breakthrough services including the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud, and Apple TV.
Apple’s more than 150,000 employees are dedicated to making the best products on earth and to leaving the world better than we found it.
iPad mini supports both Apple Pencil (USB-C) and Apple Pencil Pro, giving users two incredible options to bring their ideas to life.

Siri AI can draw on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their personal messages, emails, photos, and more; use onscreen awareness to take action related to the content on a user’s screen; and answer questions about virtually any topic.
Additionally, Apple Intelligence makes apps smarter and more useful.
Users can improve a photo’s composition after it’s been taken using tools such as upgraded Clean Up, Spatial Reframing, and Extend.
And now the all-new Image Playground app offers photorealistic imagery.
In Safari, Notify Me helps users monitor web pages for changes, like product restocks or price drops, and stay on top of updates.
Apple Intelligence uses on-device processing and Private Cloud Compute to help protect users’ privacy.

The Acoustic Display also features a sealed enclosure that helps iPad mini achieve its IP67 rating.

For parents and families looking for more information on how to help create safer, more enriching digital experiences for their kids, Apple also has a website with details on the latest tools and how to get started using them.

passages: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.

extraction.body: Microsoft is offering buyouts to around 60,000 employees across India, the US, the UK and Canada, its second voluntary exit programme this year and a much wider one than the first. Announced on Monday in a memo from Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, the Voluntary Exit Offer (VEO) covers more than a quarter of the company's roughly 223,000 employees. It reaches up to level 70 on Microsoft's internal scale, which takes in general managers and some staff with vice president titles, though not corporate vice presidents.Unlike the retirement buyout Microsoft ran earlier this year, this one has no age or tenure cut-off, and performance plays no part in who qualifies. Eligible employees will get an email with their individual terms within hours. They have until the first week of December to decide, and those who accept will leave at the end of the year."This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support," Coleman wrote. It also gives participating organisations "another way to adapt their workforce to changing needs," she added.Microsoft's voluntary exit offer pays out like its standard severanceThe package matches Microsoft's standard severance. What it leaves out is the extended healthcare that made the retirement programme an easy yes for many long-serving staff.Severance in Microsoft's US layoffs earlier this year started at 60 days of base pay and went up to 39 weeks for most employees. Staff at level 64 and below got a week of base pay for every six months of service, while levels 65 to 67 got two weeks.Not every team is in. Business leaders decide whether their groups participate, and sales is sitting this one out. Marketing, commercial business, security, and discovery and quantum teams are excluded too, according to people familiar with the matter. Copilot, CoreAI, Windows + Devices, Xbox, finance and HR are among those taking part, while Cloud + AI and Microsoft AI are partially in.Buyouts now sit alongside layoffs in Microsoft's AI-era job cutsThe VEO builds on the Voluntary Retirement Program from this spring, the first in Microsoft's history. That offer went to roughly 8,750 US employees at senior director level and below whose age and years at the company added up to at least 70. About 30% took it, and Microsoft booked a $900 million charge for it in April.The turnout helped shrink the layoffs that followed, Coleman said later. Microsoft still cut 4,800 jobs in July, about 2% of its workforce, and several hundred more in September, after cutting over 15,000 in 2025. Headcount stood at 223,000 on June 30, down from 228,000 a year earlier.The company is under pressure to hold down operating costs while it spends tens of billions on data centres and AI infrastructure. Still, Microsoft says the buyout is not a sign it needs fewer people, nor a replacement for layoffs, which remain on the table. It expects a much smaller share of employees to accept this time.Quarterly earnings on Wednesday could offer a first look at what the offer will cost. Coleman called the programme "new for us" in her memo, and said in July that Microsoft was studying whether voluntary exits could become a regular, even annual, fixture. How many of these 60,000 employees take the deal will likely settle that.You use AI every day.

coreStoryFacts.text: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, or about 27% of its global workforce, as the company spends heavily on artificial intelligence.

Amy Coleman wrote in a blog post that “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us,” and she said Microsoft would “keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.” Microsoft said the voluntary exit offer was available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, and the company said employees must be at the vice president level or below to qualify.

Microsoft told Business Insider that eligible employees will have until early December to decide whether to take the offer and exit at the end of the year, and a Microsoft spokesperson said there are no plans for another buyout at this time.
Participants receive severance packages and career-planning resources.

Microsoft’s buyout offers are individualized based on an employee’s level, location, and tenure, and employees at internal levels 64 and below were offered one week of base pay per six months of service.
Microsoft’s capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, and in the same quarter a year ago capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion.
Microsoft is preparing a massive exodus of workers and inviting 60,000 people to leave in a gigantic voluntary departure.
Microsoft opens the door to voluntary departures to trim the workforce quietly: offering money to employees to leave the company on their own terms.

story.title: Microsoft offers to buy out a quarter of its workforce

facts.text: On Monday, Microsoft said it will offer voluntary buyouts to eligible employees in select parts of the company.
CNBC reports that the buyouts will be offered to roughly 60,000 employees , or about a quarter of its global workforce.
The company describes the offer as an opportunity for employees who may have already been considering career moves outside Microsoft.

While Microsoft did not give a direct reason for the buyout package, it comes as the company has spent the last several years managing costs amid investment in AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
The effort is the second time Microsoft has run a voluntary workforce reduction in 2026.
In April, the company offered its first voluntary retirement package to 8,750 US employees.
Microsoft will extend the voluntary exit offer (VEO) to qualifying employees in the United States, India, Canada, and the United Kingdom.

The company’s employee rankings are internal, but according to the salary and career database Levels.fyi , levels 65–67 correspond to principal positions, and 68–70 are at the partner/distinguished level.
According to Chief People Officer Amy Coleman, eligible organizations were selected “based on each business’s priorities, customer commitments and workforce needs.”
While layoffs remain the most common way to reduce headcounts in the tech world, Microsoft may be following Google’s playbook.
As Business Insider reported, Alphabet offered employees voluntary exit packages in June and October 2025, and again in February 2026.
Now, eligible Microsoft employees may have to decide whether to take a deal now or keep their jobs and face the uncertainty of future company-wide layoffs.
In comments to GeekWire in July, Coleman said Microsoft was looking into making voluntary exits part of workforce management more regularly.
She described the current VEO as something that “builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program.”
According to Microsoft’s blog , employees eligible for the VEO will be contacted via email on Monday.
Microsoft will announce its latest earnings after market close later this week.
Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, or about 27% of its global workforce, as the company spends heavily on artificial intelligence.

Amy Coleman wrote in a blog post that “The Voluntary Exit Offer is new for us,” and she said Microsoft would “keep helping people focus on the work that matters most, build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across Microsoft.” Microsoft said the voluntary exit offer was available to eligible employees in Canada, India, the United Kingdom and the United States, and the company said employees must be at the vice president level or below to qualify.
Participants receive severance packages and career-planning resources.

Microsoft’s buyout offers are individualized based on an employee’s level, location, and tenure, and employees at internal levels 64 and below were offered one week of base pay per six months of service.
Microsoft’s capital expenditures for the September quarter should exceed $50 billion, and in the same quarter a year ago capital spending and finance leases came to $34.9 billion.

extraction.body: Just as rumors last week suggested, the redesigned 8th-generation iPad Mini (2026) has arrived ahead of Apple's "Pro and Tell" event on Wednesday, October 28th. The refreshed pint-sized tablet features a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the A20 Pro chip, an improved front-facing camera, and, for the first time on any iPad, IP67 water and dust resistance. The redesigned pint-sized tablet also features a less thick 5.4mm design and 24% thinner bezels. On the display front, the new 8.5-inch OLED screen offers 2x higher peak brightness at 1,200 nits (along with 1 nit minimum brightness), plus a nano-texture display option similar to recent iPad Pro releases. However, the new iPad Mini still doesn't feature a 120Hz ProMotion display and is locked to 60Hz. The 2024-released 7th-generation iPad Mini featured an 8.3-inch LCD screen with relatively thick bezels. The larger OLED panel should deliver deeper blacks, improved contrast, and more vibrant colors. At the same time, the tablet might also have worse battery life, since OLED panel technology consumes more power, though efficiency improvements in the A20 Pro could offset that. In the press release, Apple says that the new iPad Mini can hit 10 hours of battery life while watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi. Regarding the A20 Pro specifically, the chip features a 5-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, making it compatible with Apple's new Siri AI features, including the assistant's more expressive voice. It also has a 7-core GPU that delivers up to 2.7x faster graphics performance. Lastly, the 512GB model features a 6-core CPU. The tablet's front-facing camera has been upgraded to a 12-megapixel Center Stage shooter that sits on its landscape bezel edge. Other upgrades include the Acoustic Display, which Apple says features "specially designed woofers" that are "paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume." Lastly, the tablet features Apple's C2 cellular modem (if you opt for the cellular version), alongside its N1 wireless chip. Apple says the new iPad Mini will be available to pre-order on Wednesday, October 28th, starting at $700, with availability launching on November 6th. While the 8th-gen iPad Mini seems like a solid all-around upgrade thanks to the A20 Pro chip and the new OLED panel, it's a bit crazy that it starts at $700, especially since the last refresh in 2024 launched at $500 (which already felt pretty expensive). Later this week, Apple is expected to reveal a touch-screen MacBook Pro and the M6-powered MacBook Pro and iPad. New features include more accurate health tracking and longer battery life.

It increases the screen size while reducing thickness and weight, and significantly strengthens AI performance.On Oct. 26 (local time), Apple announced the eighth-generation iPad mini ahead of its "Pro and tell" event on Oct. It cuts bezels by 24 percent from the previous version, keeping the body size the same while expanding the screen from 8.3 inches to 8.5 inches.The display supports up to 1,200 nits of peak brightness and a 2 million-to-1 contrast ratio. Minimum brightness is 1 nit for more comfortable use in dark environments. The refresh rate is 60 Hz and it does not support the 120 Hz ProMotion feature.Thickness is 5.4 mm, 0.9 mm thinner than the previous model. Weight drops to 255 grams from 293 grams, and it adds IP67-rated water and dust resistance for the first time on an iPad mini.The key change is the A20 Pro chip. Apple said AI processing performance is up to 4.5 times higher than the previous model, and graphics performance is up to 2.7 times higher. It supports running on-device AI models and can use new Siri AI features in iPadOS 27.Its audio system applies an acoustic display that uses the display to boost bass and volume. The 12-megapixel front camera moves to the landscape edge to improve convenience for video calls. It includes Apple-designed N1 wireless chip to support Wi-Fi 7, and the cellular model uses the C2 modem.It comes in two colors: Midnight and Starlight. Storage options are 128GB, 256GB and 512GB, and the top two models can choose a nano-texture display that reduces light reflection.In the United States, prices start at $699 for the Wi-Fi model (1,149,000 won in South Korea) and $849 for the cellular model (1,399,000 won in South Korea).

Leading up to its "pro and tell" event later this week, Apple kicked off its latest round of announcements by revealing the new iPad mini . The 8th-generation small tablet now comes with an 8.5-inch OLED display, a longstanding wish list item for many mini fans. The new tablet also gains an updated A20 Pro processor, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a nano-texture option for the display. It starts at $699, $100 more than the previous version, and will be available for pre-order on Oct. 28. Apple has been slow to update the iPad mini over the years, much to the chagrin of its niche yet vocal fanbase . The previous generation came out in 2024, adding more storage, Apple Pencil support and a processor upgrade. The version before that came out in 2021 and finally removed the aging Home button from the tiny tablet. Apple has spent more time updating other iPad models, including the entry-level iPad and iPad Pro lineup. The latter received OLED screens in 2024, so the inclusion of that technology on the latest iPad mini now is noteworthy. Why are fans so keen on an OLED iPad mini? OLED displays offer better contrast and deeper blacks, resulting in higher-quality images overall. Flagship smartphones like the iPhone 18 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 use OLED screens too, so updating the iPad mini to have the same technology will make it look and feel more modern. But most popular smartphones also have 120Hz refresh rates, which makes scrolling feel quicker and smoother. Apple appears to have skipped this on the new iPad mini (no refresh rate is listed in the new iPad mini's specs; we've reached out to Apple to confirm) and that will likely be a deal breaker for some who find the standard 60Hz to feel too sluggish in comparison. There's also the argument that one could simply get an iPhone Duo now, which has similar dimensions to the iPad mini when unfolded, along with an OLED screen and a 120Hz refresh rate. But the iPhone Duo costs $2,000, and it seems to be having some unique issues of its own at the moment, just days after its official launch. The new iPad mini's A20 Pro processor should give it a decent performance boost, while the 12MP Center Stage camera on its landscape edge should make it more convenient to make FaceTime video calls. The nano-texture display option appears similar to that of the iPhone Duo's inner display, which is designed to reduce glare. Note, though, that this feature is optional on the iPad mini, is only available on the 256GB and 512GB storage options and bumps up the final price by an additional $100. Pre-orders open for the new iPad mini on Oct. 28, and it will be widely available starting Nov. 6.

The new iPad mini has roughly the same footprint as the 2024 release, but the display is slightly larger thanks to a 24 percent reduction in bezel thickness. The device is almost a full millimeter thinner than the last iPad, coming in at just 5.4 mm. The chassis is also IP67 rated for water and dust protection. The 7th-Gen iPad mini didn’t have any official IP rating. The 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display (up from 8.3 inches) moves on from the IPS technology of the last-gen device to adopt OLED. That means dapper blacks and a much higher peak brightness—1,200 nits versus just 500 nits for the previous mini. It can also manage 1-nit minimum brightness so as not to sear your retinas in a dark room. There will also be a nano-textured matte display option. The display experience on the new mini should be much more in line with what we’ve come to expect from Apple’s Pro-level devices. The 2-nanometer A20 Pro chip was a noticeable upgrade in the iPhone 18 Pro , and it will be even more significant in this tablet. The previous model had a 3-nanometer A17 Pro chip, which was already a year old when it appeared in the iPad mini. In the iPhone 18 Pro, we found the A20 Pro significantly improved graphics performance thanks in part to a 50 percent increase in memory bandwidth. Higher memory speed also helps with on-device AI applications, but the Neural Engine is the primary factor. Unfortunately, not all versions of the new iPad mini will be equally capable. Apple notes the 512GB configuration will have the dual 16-core Neural Engine we saw in the iPhone 18 Pro, but the 128GB and 256GB versions will have a single 16-core NPU. These versions will also have a slightly different CPU configuration, with five cores instead of six. Apple has retained the 12 MP cameras for the front and back of the tablet, but the front-facing one has changed location. Rather than being on the short edge for portrait-orientation video calls, it’s now on the long edge. That might take a little getting used to for those who frequently use their tablets for FaceTime. The $699 base price gets you 128GB of storage and Wi-Fi connectivity. It’s $100 more for 256GB and $300 more for 512GB. The nano-texture display is also a $100 upsell, but it’s only available for the 256GB and 512GB versions. The step up to cellular will cost $849 for the 128GB model. Pricing is, sadly, not eye-popping for 2026, but it marks yet another price increase for Apple. The 7th-gen iPad mini launched for $499 in 2024, but it has since risen to $599. The new model adds $100, but it does have some nice upgrades. Preorders for the new iPad mini begin at 10:10 am PT on October 28 (Wednesday), and devices will arrive on doorsteps and in stores on November 6. However, the new iPad Mini still doesn't feature a 120Hz ProMotion display and is locked to 60Hz. The 2024-released 7th-generation iPad Mini featured an 8.3-inch LCD screen with relatively thick bezels. The larger OLED panel should deliver deeper blacks, improved contrast, and more vibrant colors. At the same time, the tablet might also have worse battery life, since OLED panel technology consumes more power, though efficiency improvements in the A20 Pro could offset that. In the press release, Apple says that the new iPad Mini can hit 10 hours of battery life while watching videos or browsing the web on Wi-Fi. Regarding the A20 Pro specifically, the chip features a 5-core CPU with two super cores and three efficiency cores, making it compatible with Apple's new Siri AI features, including the assistant's more expressive voice. It also has a 7-core GPU that delivers up to 2.7x faster graphics performance. Lastly, the 512GB model features a 6-core CPU. The tablet's front-facing camera has been upgraded to a 12-megapixel Center Stage shooter that sits on its landscape bezel edge. Other upgrades include the Acoustic Display, which Apple says features "specially designed woofers" that are "paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume." Lastly, the tablet features Apple's C2 cellular modem (if you opt for the cellular version), alongside its N1 wireless chip. Apple says the new iPad Mini will be available to pre-order on Wednesday, October 28th, starting at $700, with availability launching on November 6th. While the 8th-gen iPad Mini seems like a solid all-around upgrade thanks to the A20 Pro chip and the new OLED panel, it's a bit crazy that it starts at $700, especially since the last refresh in 2024 launched at $500 (which already felt pretty expensive). Later this week, Apple is expected to reveal a touch-screen MacBook Pro and the M6-powered MacBook Pro and iPad. New features include more accurate health tracking and longer battery life.

Leading up to its "pro and tell" event later this week, Apple kicked off its latest round of announcements by revealing the new iPad mini . The 8th-generation small tablet now comes with an 8.5-inch OLED display, a longstanding wish list item for many mini fans. The new tablet also gains an updated A20 Pro processor, a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera and a nano-texture option for the display. It starts at $699, $100 more than the previous version, and will be available for pre-order on Oct. 28. Apple has been slow to update the iPad mini over the years, much to the chagrin of its niche yet vocal fanbase . The previous generation came out in 2024, adding more storage, Apple Pencil support and a processor upgrade. The version before that came out in 2021 and finally removed the aging Home button from the tiny tablet. Apple has spent more time updating other iPad models, including the entry-level iPad and iPad Pro lineup. The latter received OLED screens in 2024, so the inclusion of that technology on the latest iPad mini now is noteworthy. Why are fans so keen on an OLED iPad mini? OLED displays offer better contrast and deeper blacks, resulting in higher-quality images overall. Flagship smartphones like the iPhone 18 Pro and Samsung Galaxy S26 use OLED screens too, so updating the iPad mini to have the same technology will make it look and feel more modern. But most popular smartphones also have 120Hz refresh rates, which makes scrolling feel quicker and smoother. Apple appears to have skipped this on the new iPad mini (no refresh rate is listed in the new iPad mini's specs; we've reached out to Apple to confirm) and that will likely be a deal breaker for some who find the standard 60Hz to feel too sluggish in comparison. There's also the argument that one could simply get an iPhone Duo now, which has similar dimensions to the iPad mini when unfolded, along with an OLED screen and a 120Hz refresh rate. But the iPhone Duo costs $2,000, and it seems to be having some unique issues of its own at the moment, just days after its official launch. The new iPad mini's A20 Pro processor should give it a decent performance boost, while the 12MP Center Stage camera on its landscape edge should make it more convenient to make FaceTime video calls. The nano-texture display option appears similar to that of the iPhone Duo's inner display, which is designed to reduce glare. Note, though, that this feature is optional on the iPad mini, is only available on the 256GB and 512GB storage options and bumps up the final price by an additional $100. Pre-orders open for the new iPad mini on Oct. 28, and it will be widely available starting Nov. 6.

story.title: Apple reveals updated iPad mini with a bigger OLED screen for $700

facts.text: The iPhone Duo may be a bit of a risk right now , but there’s a new mid-size Apple touchscreen device that might do the job.
Starting at $699, the 8th-gen iPad mini price has gone up, but there are some big changes.
Higher memory speed also helps with on-device AI applications, but the Neural Engine is the primary factor.
Unfortunately, not all versions of the new iPad mini will be equally capable.
These versions will also have a slightly different CPU configuration, with five cores instead of six.
Apple claims this is the most significant update ever for the iPad mini line.
The 8.5-inch Super Retina XDR display (up from 8.3 inches) moves on from the IPS technology of the last-gen device to adopt OLED.
That means dapper blacks and a much higher peak brightness—1,200 nits versus just 500 nits for the previous mini.
It can also manage 1-nit minimum brightness so as not to sear your retinas in a dark room.
There will also be a nano-textured matte display option.
The display experience on the new mini should be much more in line with what we’ve come to expect from Apple’s Pro-level devices.
Apple has retained the 12 MP cameras for the front and back of the tablet, but the front-facing one has changed location.
Rather than being on the short edge for portrait-orientation video calls, it’s now on the long edge.
That might take a little getting used to for those who frequently use their tablets for FaceTime.

sources.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant
passages: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models.

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers.
The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how.
For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.
He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers.

extraction.body: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done. Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding. He recalled celebrating when his wife started leaving her computer on all night so that her agents could keep working. “On the product team, what I think about is, how do we make this intuitive and useful to people?” he told Disrupt attendees. “A lot of that isn’t building some new piece of tech into the product; it’s how you frame it to the user and how it feels.” Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers. For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it. In our testing, the assistant’s ability to think ahead is apparent and often useful, but it isn’t quite there yet. It will flag calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines, but not necessarily in the most timely fashion. “The first time it told me about one of those [conflicts]—this is like early in development—it told me three minutes before the thing,” Embiricos says of his dot. “It’s like, ‘Hey, this thing is coming up. You might want to do something about it.’ I only have three minutes!” Embiricos expects the timing to improve over time, but the proactive approach is key to the product. “I was hearing about an engineer at a drone delivery startup, and they were saying, ‘We had this outage, and by the time I noticed that the outage was going on, my dot had already noticed the outage was happening, had already analyzed the outage, and had come to me with useful information for how we could resolve the outage.’” As with most AI agent use cases, there’s a tension between the personal information an AI model needs to be useful and exactly how much personal data you are exposing to a software company. Muse has been criticized for the profiles it builds of your family and friends, which the software uses to know, say, what kind of restaurant you might want to go to with a specific pal, but could also add incredible value to Meta’s advertising business. Hark, a start-up developing its own AI personal assistant, is explicit in pointing out it that it doesn’t collect data to fuel an advertising business the way that OpenAI and Meta do. With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how. Still, those controls aren’t granular and the app can be pushy. For example, it refuses to accept read-only access to cloud drives. “What I think we need to do is basically build out super, super, super granular controls,” Embiricos said, but he pointed to the model’s intelligence and discretion as the other side of this coin. “This is actually something we kind of got some flack about when we launched,” Embiricos said. “We had really conservative defaults over what the agent would do, and it would ask for permission a lot. I remember knowing that we were going to see that feedback, but thinking, ‘This is okay, we can tune that over time.’” The other big question about AI agents is whether they can scale. They’re fun when only a few people have them, and stories of agents snagging hard-to-get reservations abound. But businesses don’t necessarily like dealing with agents and might not be equipped to. People certainly don’t like dealing with them (note: stop having your AI agents pitch me), and Embiricos is among those people. He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.” If the AI industry is right that agents are our future, can we get there without overwhelming the infrastructure that our world currently runs on, from businesses and websites to payment networks? “At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem. Giving an assistant access to my email inbox already feels like a big ask, but my bank account is off limits. For now.

sources.title: OpenAI launches dots, an always-on agentic assistant - The News International
passages: OpenAI used its Dev Day event on Tuesday to unveil Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra.
The company describes the agents as capable, always-on systems built to handle tasks continuously with minimal supervision.
It was stated that OpenAI is currently collaborating with Microsoft to incorporate Dots within Agent 365, which is Microsoft's framework for enterprise AI agents.

OpenAI framed the launch as an evolving system, describing plans for users to eventually deploy multiple Dots working together on their behalf, starting with a single primary Dot that can be named and customised.
OpenAI also confirmed users will be able to message their Dots through workplace platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams, with text message support planned for a future update.
Specialist Dots, where each dot is assigned an identity, credentials, and certain tools according to its function, is another thing that OpenAI brings forward.

sources.title: OpenAI Unveils Always-On AI Agent Dots to Chase Meta's Muse
passages: SILICON VALLEY/BEIJING — OpenAI unveiled Dots, an artificial intelligence agent that runs around the clock, setting up a fierce rivalry with Meta's Muse.
OpenAI countered with its coding tool Codex, only to face another challenge on the 8th of this month when Meta introduced Muse, a free personal agent.
Chinese companies, spurred by Muse's popularity, are rolling out agents of their own, extending the U.S.-China AI contest from large language models into the market for agents.
Muse, backed by social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that draw more than 3 billion active users a day, overtook ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app.
Meta also expanded Muse to small and mid-sized businesses on the same day, signaling that it is targeting corporate customers as well as individual users.
OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman introduced Dots on the 29th at DevDay 2026, the company's annual developer conference, held at the Fort Mason Center in San Francisco.
Dots runs on GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most advanced model, giving it strong performance.
OpenAI engineers are using Dots to fix dozens of software bugs a day.
The arrival of Dots is expected to intensify competition among agents.
OpenAI led the chatbot market after launching ChatGPT in November 2022, but lost the initiative early this year when rival Anthropic released enterprise AI and coding tools.
OpenAI will offer Dots first to users of its enterprise products and subscribers to ChatGPT Pro, its higher-tier plan, and plans to widen access over time.
Alibaba has been expanding its AI chatbot Qwen since November last year into a personal assistant that performs real tasks by linking to shopping, travel and mobile payment services.

extraction.body: OpenAI launched Dots on September 29, turning ChatGPT into an always-on agent that can keep working after a conversation ends. The OpenAI Dots agent has a friendly avatar, a customizable name, and enough access to order dinner. Yet its design, permissions, and strongest early results point firmly toward workplace software. That tension matters because consumer agents usually compete on convenience. Meta’s Muse and similar products promise a personal shopper, travel planner, and universal checkout assistant. coreStoryFacts.text: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models.

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers.
The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how.
For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.
He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers.
OpenAI used its Dev Day event on Tuesday to unveil Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra.
The company describes the agents as capable, always-on systems built to handle tasks continuously with minimal supervision.
It was stated that OpenAI is currently collaborating with Microsoft to incorporate Dots within Agent 365, which is Microsoft's framework for enterprise AI agents.

OpenAI framed the launch as an evolving system, describing plans for users to eventually deploy multiple Dots working together on their behalf, starting with a single primary Dot that can be named and customised.
OpenAI also confirmed users will be able to message their Dots through workplace platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams, with text message support planned for a future update.
Specialist Dots, where each dot is assigned an identity, credentials, and certain tools according to its function, is another thing that OpenAI brings forward.
SILICON VALLEY/BEIJING — OpenAI unveiled Dots, an artificial intelligence agent that runs around the clock, setting up a fierce rivalry with Meta's Muse.
OpenAI countered with its coding tool Codex, only to face another challenge on the 8th of this month when Meta introduced Muse, a free personal agent.
Chinese companies, spurred by Muse's popularity, are rolling out agents of their own, extending the U.S.-China AI contest from large language models into the market for agents.
Muse, backed by social media platforms including Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp that draw more than 3 billion active users a day, overtook ChatGPT to become the most downloaded app.
Meta also expanded Muse to small and mid-sized businesses on the same day, signaling that it is targeting corporate customers as well as individual users.
OpenAI Chief Executive Sam Altman introduced Dots on the 29th at DevDay 2026, the company's annual developer conference, held at the Fort Mason Center in San Francisco.
Dots runs on GPT-6 Astra, OpenAI's most advanced model, giving it strong performance.
OpenAI engineers are using Dots to fix dozens of software bugs a day.
The arrival of Dots is expected to intensify competition among agents.
OpenAI led the chatbot market after launching ChatGPT in November 2022, but lost the initiative early this year when rival Anthropic released enterprise AI and coding tools.

extraction.body: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models. The startup Instinct became an overnight sensation, and Meta put the full force of its marketing behind its assistant, Muse. OpenAI wasn’t going to be left out. The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September. Alexander Embiricos, who leads OpenAI’s enterprise product team, joined us at TechCrunch Disrupt this month to explain where the product came from—starting with the question of why so many companies seem to be turning to cutesy mascots as avatars for their trillion-parameter matrix multiplication machines. “There’s kind of this convergent evolution happening,” Embiricos said of the efforts to build AI assistants. “As we were working on the product, we realized if we could frame this as, it’s an entity and it’s a single conversation, not many different conversations….it starts to become intuitive.” The assistant is available in the ChatGPT desktop and mobile apps to subscribers on the Pro tier or higher, with plans starting at $100 a month. Once it is connected to your calendar, email, computer and other tools, the agent tries to help you get your work done. Embiricos points out that you could achieve much of dots’ functionality with Open AI’s Codex app, its coding tool, released at the beginning of this year. But that requires more work and hand-holding. He recalled celebrating when his wife started leaving her computer on all night so that her agents could keep working. “On the product team, what I think about is, how do we make this intuitive and useful to people?” he told Disrupt attendees. “A lot of that isn’t building some new piece of tech into the product; it’s how you frame it to the user and how it feels.” Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers. Even the name—a play on the negative space inside of OpenAI’s logo—is intended “to feel like just something that could eventually be ubiquitous.” (Asked when he learned that rival AI entrepreneur Elon Musk owns the dot.com URL, Embiricos said, “I found out very late.”) The idea of a persistent agent is that it doesn’t need prompting. For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it. In our testing, the assistant’s ability to think ahead is apparent and often useful, but it isn’t quite there yet. It will flag calendar conflicts and upcoming deadlines, but not necessarily in the most timely fashion. “The first time it told me about one of those [conflicts]—this is like early in development—it told me three minutes before the thing,” Embiricos says of his dot. “It’s like, ‘Hey, this thing is coming up. You might want to do something about it.’ I only have three minutes!” Embiricos expects the timing to improve over time, but the proactive approach is key to the product. “I was hearing about an engineer at a drone delivery startup, and they were saying, ‘We had this outage, and by the time I noticed that the outage was going on, my dot had already noticed the outage was happening, had already analyzed the outage, and had come to me with useful information for how we could resolve the outage.’” As with most AI agent use cases, there’s a tension between the personal information an AI model needs to be useful and exactly how much personal data you are exposing to a software company. Muse has been criticized for the profiles it builds of your family and friends, which the software uses to know, say, what kind of restaurant you might want to go to with a specific pal, but could also add incredible value to Meta’s advertising business. Does dots collect similar data? “Yes, we have a thing that we built into dots, which we call proactive research,” Embiricos said. “On a cadence, it will think about what it knows about you, what is the conversation that it’s had, and then what have you given it access to that it can think about, and then it will go and research, ‘What could I do to be more helpful to you?’ And then, basically, it will propose that.” It’s difficult to separate the data needs of the agent from that of its parent corporation. Hark, a start-up developing its own AI personal assistant, is explicit in pointing out it that it doesn’t collect data to fuel an advertising business the way that OpenAI and Meta do. With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how. Still, those controls aren’t granular and the app can be pushy. For example, it refuses to accept read-only access to cloud drives. “What I think we need to do is basically build out super, super, super granular controls,” Embiricos said, but he pointed to the model’s intelligence and discretion as the other side of this coin. “This is actually something we kind of got some flack about when we launched,” Embiricos said. “We had really conservative defaults over what the agent would do, and it would ask for permission a lot. I remember knowing that we were going to see that feedback, but thinking, ‘This is okay, we can tune that over time.’” The other big question about AI agents is whether they can scale. They’re fun when only a few people have them, and stories of agents snagging hard-to-get reservations abound. But businesses don’t necessarily like dealing with agents and might not be equipped to. People certainly don’t like dealing with them (note: stop having your AI agents pitch me), and Embiricos is among those people. He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.” If the AI industry is right that agents are our future, can we get there without overwhelming the infrastructure that our world currently runs on, from businesses and websites to payment networks? “At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem. I probably can’t say too much here, but we’re deep in lots of conversations with payment processors.” Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers. Giving an assistant access to my email inbox already feels like a big ask, but my bank account is off limits. For now.
