extraction.body: OpenAI launched Dots on September 29, turning ChatGPT into an always-on agent that can keep working after a conversation ends. The OpenAI Dots agent has a friendly avatar, a customizable name, and enough access to order dinner. Yet its design, permissions, and strongest early results point firmly toward workplace software. That tension matters because consumer agents usually compete on convenience. Meta’s Muse and similar products promise a personal shopper, travel planner, and universal checkout assistant. OpenAI instead gives its agent a cloud computer, connected applications, optional local computer access, and controls that resemble an IT administration console. The difference becomes clear when Dots meets the open web. It can search email, prepare a purchase, or navigate a service, but security checks often force the user back into control. Give it a website, media files, or another environment you manage, and the product starts looking much more capable. OpenAI is therefore testing a larger proposition than automated dinner orders. It wants people and companies to delegate ongoing responsibilities to software that can remember context, operate applications, and return completed work. The cute character is the invitation. The real product is an autonomous coworker. Dots changes ChatGPT from a destination for questions into a worker that can retain responsibility for an unfinished goal. OpenAI introduced Dots during DevDay 2026 in San Francisco. The company describes a dot as an always-on agent powered by GPT-6 Astra. An agent is software that can plan and perform several actions toward a goal, rather than only generating a response. Each dot receives its own cloud computer. It can use websites, run applications, consult connected services, and continue making progress between conversations. Users can inspect its activity, redirect it, or stop it while work is underway. Its interface presents the dot as a personable character. Users choose a name and interact through chat or voice. A separate view exposes the cloud computer, letting the owner watch the agent navigate software and websites. That visual approach resembles Meta Muse, but the underlying framing differs. Muse presents the agent as an approachable personal helper. Dots looks more like a managed workstation operated by an AI employee. The distinction appears in OpenAI’s enterprise controls. Workspace administrators can enable or disable Dots, connected applications, cloud browsing, network access, and local computer control. They can also decide whether members may add their agents to workplace messaging systems. Enterprise access starts disabled by default. Local computer access and customizable action rules also require separate permission. According to OpenAI’s workspace controls , enabling the agent does not automatically grant every connected service or computer capability. Those settings reveal OpenAI’s intended destination. Ordering food makes an accessible demonstration, but administering autonomous software requires identity, permission, auditability, and policy. Those are enterprise requirements. The persistence also changes how users must formulate requests. A dot works best with a responsibility, relevant context, and clear boundaries. “Keep this project moving” fits the design better than a disconnected sequence of small prompts. This is close to an AI workflow , where information, decisions, and repeated actions remain connected over time. The agent becomes valuable when it can carry context across those steps. That is the first reversal behind Dots. OpenAI wrapped a serious delegation system in a charming character. The personality makes the software approachable, but its operational model belongs in the workplace. The most important contrast is not OpenAI against Meta as companies. It is managed delegation against consumer convenience. Consumer agents sell a simple idea. Ask for an outcome, watch the software cross several websites, and approve the final transaction. Shopping, reservations, travel planning, and personal scheduling are natural demonstrations because everyone understands the friction. OpenAI can support those scenarios. In one company demonstration, a dot noticed that its user would work through dinner. It then prepared two delivery choices, including estimated costs, and asked which meal should be ordered. That demonstration made the agent feel personal and proactive. However, OpenAI devoted substantial product architecture to responsibilities that extend far beyond a meal. Dots can use workplace applications, retain project context, access a local machine, and eventually divide work among multiple agents. The company has also discussed specialist dots for enterprise customers. These agents would focus on defined areas such as accounting, marketing, or legal analysis. A specialist structure assumes organizations will assign responsibilities, evaluate outputs, and govern access by role. Ordering dinner has a lower ceiling. Saving several minutes is useful, but a security challenge or failed login can erase the benefit. A person who must repeatedly rescue an agent may return to the ordinary app. The consumer and enterprise routes also face different business pressures. A mass-market assistant must reach many users and find a sustainable commercial model. A workplace agent can justify itself through completed projects, reduced delays, or expanded capacity. Neither route guarantees reliable performance. Enterprise environments contain sensitive information and consequential actions. Their structured software may help an agent operate, but mistakes can carry greater costs. OpenAI appears to be betting that governance can make broader access acceptable. Administrators can restrict capabilities, while users can define custom rules for supported actions. Sensitive steps can trigger approval or require the person to take over. The cute avatar softens that administrative reality. It encourages conversation and makes delegation feel less like configuring an automation server. However, the agent’s usefulness still depends on careful setup. Dots therefore pressures both sides of the market. Consumer agents must show that convenience remains valuable when websites resist automation. Enterprise platforms must make controls usable without turning every task into a compliance project. OpenAI’s strongest advantage may be the connection between those worlds. The same agent can receive a casual voice instruction, search business context, operate software, and send progress updates to a phone. That continuity is more significant than the avatar. Disconnecting an external service stops new access. It does not automatically remove information already incorporated into the dot’s context. That behavior deserves attention before users connect broad archives. Data treatment also varies by account type and settings. OpenAI says it does not use Business, Enterprise, or Edu workspace data for model training by default. Personal accounts rely on the user’s model-improvement setting. The company’s privacy guidance says limited human review can still occur in safety-related circumstances. Users should read those controls before placing confidential material inside an agent’s working context. This creates a contest over the primary work interface. If users begin a project with their dot, individual applications can become resources in the background. If platform vendors keep agents inside their suites, ChatGPT remains one tool among many. OpenAI is preparing for both possibilities. Dots can communicate through Slack and Microsoft Teams, while enterprise administrators retain controls over access. The company has also discussed integration with Microsoft’s agent management systems. The long-term vision includes teams of dots. That idea raises the stakes because organizations would manage portfolios of agents, not one assistant. Agents could specialize, exchange work, and escalate decisions to people. Evidence of growing agent use also supports the timing. OpenAI reported that agentic activity represented 64 percent of combined Codex and ChatGPT output tokens among enterprise customers by June 2026. The company defines that measure using Codex activity, so it should not be read as independent market data. Still, the figure shows why OpenAI is expanding the Codex pattern. Coding agents demonstrated that users will delegate multistep work when outputs can be inspected and corrected. Dots attempts to apply that pattern beyond software development. The Verge’s description of Dots as “Codex, but for regular people” captures the strategy. Code offers structured files, tools, tests, and version control. General knowledge work lacks many of those safeguards.

story.title: How OpenAI turned its coding tools into dots, an always-on personal assistant

facts.text: The always-on AI personal assistant, which keeps working in the background even when you aren’t asking it to, is this year’s answer to the question of how people will actually use deep learning models.

Making the technology feel intuitive meant repackaging the functionality of the company’s models into something more accessible, a path it was already on as it spun ChatGPT Work out of the agentic coding tools it had built for software engineers.
The company released dots , its assistant offering, at its developer day in late September.

With dots, OpenAI says that the agent has the same privacy controls as ChatGPT itself: Users can turn off model training (stopping OpenAI from using their conversations to improve its AI), and control what resources it accesses within your computer and how.
For OpenAI, means more token usage, and for users, a more pro-active assistant “that’s sort of thinking about you and thinking how to help you,” as Embiricos put it.
He also has a human assistant because OpenAI’s corporate partners want to interact with a person, he said, adding, “I personally never intend to have a meeting with someone else’s agent.”

“At OpenAI…we’re not always moving the fastest in terms of shipping the next ability for the agent to work with the world,” he said. “When we do, we’re doing it really closely in collaboration with the rest of the ecosystem.
Letting an AI assistant spend money through partnerships with payment companies would be a potentially lucrative first for OpenAI, but also a big ask for consumers.
OpenAI used its Dev Day event on Tuesday to unveil Dots, a new personal agentic assistant powered by GPT-6 Astra.
The company describes the agents as capable, always-on systems built to handle tasks continuously with minimal supervision.
It was stated that OpenAI is currently collaborating with Microsoft to incorporate Dots within Agent 365, which is Microsoft's framework for enterprise AI agents.

OpenAI framed the launch as an evolving system, describing plans for users to eventually deploy multiple Dots working together on their behalf, starting with a single primary Dot that can be named and customised.
OpenAI also confirmed users will be able to message their Dots through workplace platforms like Slack and Microsoft Teams, with text message support planned for a future update.
Specialist Dots, where each dot is assigned an identity, credentials, and certain tools according to its function, is another thing that OpenAI brings forward.

extraction.body: For small businesses that need a full-featured computer without adding another bulky laptop to the travel bag, Apple is positioning its redesigned iPad mini as a mobile work tool rather than simply a compact tablet. Apple announced the new iPad mini on October 26, saying the device delivers its largest update yet. The company highlighted an 8.5-inch OLED display, a thinner and lighter design, the A20 Pro processor, faster wireless connectivity, water and dust resistance, and new artificial intelligence capabilities through iPadOS 27. Customers can pre-order the device beginning October 28, with shipments and retail availability starting November 6. Prices start at $699 for the Wi-Fi model and $849 for the Wi-Fi + Cellular version in the United States. Apple says the new model measures 5.4 millimeters thick and weighs less than its predecessor. Its IP67 rating means it can withstand dust and immersion in up to one meter of water for as long as 30 minutes under controlled laboratory conditions. That could benefit contractors checking plans outdoors, restaurant managers moving between locations, or shop owners using a tablet near sinks and work counters. However, the rating does not make the iPad mini waterproof for everyday business purposes. Apple warns that resistance can decline with normal wear and that users should not charge a wet device. Liquid damage is not covered under warranty, an important consideration for companies working in unpredictable environments. The display represents one of the more visible upgrades. Apple says the OLED panel produces deeper blacks, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. A new nano-texture option reduces glare in bright surroundings. For a photographer, designer, architect, or field technician, that could make reviewing images, diagrams, and documents easier outdoors. The nano-texture version may carry additional cost, however, and business owners should confirm pricing before budgeting for multiple employees. Performance could matter more for businesses using demanding applications. Apple claims the A20 Pro can accelerate on-device AI, local language models, photo editing, graphics work, and 3D rendering. The 512GB configuration includes a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, which Apple says doubles the processing power of the previous generation for certain AI workloads. Those claims come from Apple’s own testing, conducted in September 2026. Actual performance will depend on the software, workload, storage configuration, and whether an application processes data on the device or through the cloud. Businesses should test their core applications before replacing existing laptops or tablets across a team. The iPad mini also adds a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera positioned on the landscape edge. That arrangement could improve video calls when the tablet sits in a stand or connects to a keyboard. The rear camera supports 4K video and an Adaptive True Tone flash, which may help employees scan documents, capture inventory, record job progress, or create social media content. “iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering. “With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.” Connectivity could make the cellular version attractive to mobile businesses. Apple says its C2 modem supports up to 50 percent faster cellular data speeds than the prior model, while the N1 wireless chip enables Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and Thread. Cellular connectivity could help salespeople, inspectors, delivery operators, and service technicians stay connected away from office networks. It also adds a recurring data-plan expense, and speeds will vary by carrier, location, and network conditions. Apple’s most consequential software pitch involves artificial intelligence. Siri AI, which rolls out in beta with iPadOS 27, can use personal context, interpret onscreen information, and answer questions. Apple Intelligence also includes upgraded photo tools, Image Playground, systemwide dictation improvements, and Safari notifications for changes such as product restocks or price drops. For small businesses, those tools could reduce time spent searching through messages, rewriting notes, editing images, and monitoring web pages. Privacy may appeal to companies handling sensitive information: Apple says many requests use on-device processing or Private Cloud Compute, and that data handled through Private Cloud Compute is not stored or made accessible to Apple. Still, AI should not be treated as a substitute for review. Siri AI remains in beta, some features are unavailable in certain regions or languages, and Apple says server-based tools may face daily usage limits. Owners should also establish policies for confidential customer, employee, and financial information before allowing staff to use AI features. The tablet supports Apple Pencil USB-C for $79 and Apple Pencil Pro for $129, while the new Smart Folio costs $79. Those extras can quickly raise the total cost of ownership. A Wi-Fi model with the Pencil Pro and folio reaches $907 before taxes, and a cellular model with the same accessories reaches $1,057. Apple offers trade-in credits, installment plans, leasing, and AppleCare options. Financing can reduce the immediate cash burden, but eligibility requirements, credit approval, carrier conditions, and lease termination charges apply. Businesses should compare the full cost with a laptop, an existing tablet, or a refurbished device before committing. The new iPad mini is available in midnight and starlight finishes with 128GB, 256GB, and 512GB storage. More details are available in Apple’s original announcement . For owners who value portability and already use Apple software, the device could become a flexible tool for communication, field operations, content creation, and light productivity. For teams that rely on desktop software, extensive typing, or large screens, it may work best as a targeted mobile companion rather than a universal computer replacement. coreStoryFacts.text: Apple on Monday announced a new iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display.
The tablet features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor and is powered by an A20 Pro chip.
The tech giant revealed the new device just days before its “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday.
Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, the iPad mini has up to 4.5-times faster AI performance than the previous generation, according to Apple.
It also features an “Acoustic Display” that Apple says enhances the audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content.
Specially designed woofers integrated into the display deliver deeper bass and higher volume for richer sound, per the company.
The Super Retina XDR display uses OLED technology for pixel-level lighting control, delivering deeper blacks, richer contrast, and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vibrant colors.

“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering.

“With a remarkably thinner and lighter design, a stunning new OLED display, the incredibly powerful A20 Pro, and water and dust resistance, the new iPad mini is a huge leap forward for users who love having the full iPad experience in the palm of their hand.”

However, the rating does not make the iPad mini waterproof for everyday business purposes.

story.title: Apple unveils new iPad mini with OLED display and faster A20 Pro chip

facts.text: Apple on Monday announced a new iPad mini with a larger 8.5-inch OLED display.
The tablet features a thinner and lighter design than its predecessor and is powered by an A20 Pro chip.
The tech giant revealed the new device just days before its “Pro and Tell” event that’s scheduled to take place on Wednesday.
Powered by a 7-core GPU with Neural Accelerators in each core, the iPad mini has up to 4.5-times faster AI performance than the previous generation, according to Apple.
It also features an “Acoustic Display” that Apple says enhances the audio experience when gaming, watching videos, or editing content.
Specially designed woofers integrated into the display deliver deeper bass and higher volume for richer sound, per the company.
The Super Retina XDR display uses OLED technology for pixel-level lighting control, delivering deeper blacks, richer contrast, and support for the P3 wide color gamut for more vibrant colors.

“iPad mini is beloved for its fantastic portability, performance, and display by a wide range of users, from creators and small business owners to doctors, field service workers, and gamers,” said Dave Pakula, Apple’s vice president of Hardware Engineering.
Our mission is to bring you "Small business success … delivered daily."
However, the rating does not make the iPad mini waterproof for everyday business purposes.

For small businesses that need a full-featured computer without adding another bulky laptop to the travel bag, Apple is positioning its redesigned iPad mini as a mobile work tool rather than simply a compact tablet.
Apple says the OLED panel produces deeper blacks, a 2,000,000:1 contrast ratio, and peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits.
Apple has officially announced its new iPad mini, introducing a larger 8.5-inch OLED display, the powerful A20 Pro chip, improved cameras, and water resistance.
The redesigned tablet also features a thinner and lighter body, faster connectivity, and support for Apple’s latest AI features through iPadOS 27.
The new model measures just 5.4mm thick and carries an IP67 rating for water and dust resistance, addressing another feature previously rumored for the OLED iPad mini .

passages: If you had invested $1,000 in Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), XRP (CRYPTO:XRP), or Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) five years ago, you bought in close to the peak of a major market rally.
Bitcoin closed October 2021 at $61,340 and hit a high of $68,770 in November 2021, shortly before the market began to decline.
As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Bitcoin emerged as the top performer, yielding a 36.6% gain over five years, while XRP followed closely with a 29.5% increase.
In contrast, Ethereum and Solana are still trading significantly below their prices from October 2021.
To break even, Ethereum would need to surpass $3,954, an increase of about 70%, and Solana would need to rise above $185, about 83% higher.
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.
Even Ethereum and XRP investors faced significant losses after experiencing gains.
Unfortunately, both coins saw declines of 51.0% for XRP and 44.0% for Ethereum in the following year.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%.
However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
Bitcoin may maintain its leading position as it has gained the most of these coins since 2021.
If Bitcoin stays above $79,107 (its low in October 2026), the initial $1,000 investment keeps showing a solid profit.
However, if it falls below $58,681, that gain could disappear entirely.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Its lowest monthly price during this period was $348 in October 2022, a 24% dip—much less severe than Bitcoin's or Solana's drops.
It then surged to its all-time high in October 2025, making that stake worth around $2,150.
It plummeted to a low of $8.12 in December 2022, cutting the initial investment down to about $44, a staggering 95.6% loss.
However, it rebounded to $295 in January 2025, bringing that stake back up to about $1,597.
Of the four cryptocurrencies, two gained value while two lost almost half their value.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) tracks large U.S. companies and closed at $459 in October 2021.

passages: Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%. However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
We examined a $1,000 investment in each coin made on October 27, 2021, and evaluated their worth recently. Of the four cryptocurrencies, two gained value while two lost almost half their value.
Bitcoin turned a $1,000 investment into about $1,366, a 36.6% increase over five years. XRP closely followed with a value of approximately $1,295 after a 29.5% gain.
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.

Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.

Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.

Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

story.title: What If You Had Put $1,000 Into Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP and Solana 5 Years Ago? - 24/7 Wall St.

facts.text: If you had invested $1,000 in Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), XRP (CRYPTO:XRP), or Solana (CRYPTO:SOL) five years ago, you bought in close to the peak of a major market rally.
Bitcoin closed October 2021 at $61,340 and hit a high of $68,770 in November 2021, shortly before the market began to decline.
As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Bitcoin emerged as the top performer, yielding a 36.6% gain over five years, while XRP followed closely with a 29.5% increase.
In contrast, Ethereum and Solana are still trading significantly below their prices from October 2021.
To break even, Ethereum would need to surpass $3,954, an increase of about 70%, and Solana would need to rise above $185, about 83% higher.
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.
Even Ethereum and XRP investors faced significant losses after experiencing gains.
Unfortunately, both coins saw declines of 51.0% for XRP and 44.0% for Ethereum in the following year.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%.
However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
Bitcoin may maintain its leading position as it has gained the most of these coins since 2021.
If Bitcoin stays above $79,107 (its low in October 2026), the initial $1,000 investment keeps showing a solid profit.
However, if it falls below $58,681, that gain could disappear entirely.
Yahoo Finance is not a broker-dealer or investment adviser and does not offer securities or cryptocurrencies for sale or facilitate trading.
Its lowest monthly price during this period was $348 in October 2022, a 24% dip—much less severe than Bitcoin's or Solana's drops.
It then surged to its all-time high in October 2025, making that stake worth around $2,150.
It plummeted to a low of $8.12 in December 2022, cutting the initial investment down to about $44, a staggering 95.6% loss.
However, it rebounded to $295 in January 2025, bringing that stake back up to about $1,597.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) tracks large U.S. companies and closed at $459 in October 2021.

Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.

passages: Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

His work focuses on price levels, spot ETF flows, on-chain data and the regulatory decisions that move crypto markets, written so a first-time buyer and a seasoned trader can both use it.
Sam has written about crypto professionally since 2019 and has published more than 2,000 articles.
His analysis is syndicated on Yahoo Finance, MSN and AOL and has been cited by other crypto news sites.
He also founded MacLabs Marketing, a content and personal branding agency for crypto founders and executives.
When he isn't reading charts, Sam is usually at the gym or watching One Piece, a series he maintains has better tokenomics than most altcoins.
If you had invested $1,000 in Bitcoin ( CRYPTO:BTC ), Ethereum ( CRYPTO:ETH ), XRP ( CRYPTO:XRP ), or Solana ( CRYPTO:SOL ) five years ago, you bought in close to the peak of a major market rally.
Bitcoin closed October 2021 at $61,340 and hit a high of $68,770 in November 2021, shortly before the market began to decline.
As a result, investors bought all four cryptocurrencies near their highs.
Bitcoin emerged as the top performer, yielding a 36.6% gain over five years, while XRP followed closely with a 29.5% increase.
In contrast, Ethereum and Solana are still trading significantly below their prices from October 2021.
To break even, Ethereum would need to surpass $3,954, an increase of about 70%, and Solana would need to rise above $185, about 83% higher.
Ethereum, Solana, XRP, and Bitcoin each tell a different story heading into October, but a 64% chance of a Fed rate hike and a 5% Treasury yield could scramble the rankings before the month…
On the other hand, Ethereum fell 41.1%, reducing $1,000 to about $589, while Solana fell 45.1%, leaving about $549.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, and Solana all crashed from their 2025 peaks, but one of them stands out as having a uniquely powerful combination of factors that could fuel a sharper recovery than the others.
The reasons behind this growing divide reveal a structural problem that no wave of whale buying has yet managed…
Even Ethereum and XRP investors faced significant losses after experiencing gains.
Unfortunately, both coins saw declines of 51.0% for XRP and 44.0% for Ethereum in the following year.
Its lowest monthly price during this period was $348 in October 2022, a 24% dip—much less severe than Bitcoin’s or Solana’s drops.
Over the past 90 days, all four coins have recovered some ground, with Bitcoin up 25.6% and Solana up 37.6%.
However, they are all still significantly down compared to a year ago.
Bitcoin may maintain its leading position as it has gained the most of these coins since 2021.
If Bitcoin stays above $79,107 (its low in October 2026), the initial $1,000 investment keeps showing a solid profit.
However, if it falls below $58,681, that gain could disappear entirely.
It then surged to its all-time high in October 2025, making that stake worth around $2,150.
It plummeted to a low of $8.12 in December 2022, cutting the initial investment down to about $44, a staggering 95.6% loss.
However, it rebounded to $295 in January 2025, bringing that stake back up to about $1,597.
Of the four cryptocurrencies, two gained value while two lost almost half their value.
The SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust ( NYSEARCA:SPY ) tracks large U.S. companies and closed at $459 in October 2021.
Veteran trader Peter Brandt labeled XRP a fool coin just before a 473 million XRP treasury company prepares to hit Nasdaq, and the performance gap between XRP and its crypto rivals raises a pointed…

Anyone who put $1,000 each into Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC), Ethereum (CRYPTO: ETH), XRP (CRYPTO: XRP), and Solana (CRYPTO: SOL) at the end of October 2021 has witnessed a striking difference in how $1,000 invested in crypto has fared by October 15, 2026.
Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

Of these four investments, two have gained value while the other two have lost significant value.
Five years is just one timeframe, and different starting points can yield different results.
Even Bitcoin and XRP haven't returned to their all-time highs, with Bitcoin still far from its $126,080 peak.
This shows that which coin you choose matters more than simply investing in cryptocurrency.
Ethereum and Solana were the two most hyped coins in 2021, yet both lost money, proving excitement and network activity don't guarantee better returns.
In contrast, Ethereum dropped sharply from $4,298 to $2,426, a 44% loss that reduced the initial $1,000 investment to $564.
Both of the coins that lost money had strong appeal entering late 2021.
Ethereum was seen as the backbone of the decentralized finance (DeFi) movement and the booming NFT market (digital collectibles on the blockchain).
Solana emerged as a promising alternative, boasting high speeds and low transaction fees, attracting many buyers who believed both would outperform more established cryptocurrencies.
For investors, spreading funds across different coins may help mitigate the risks of any single investment.

Future moves could change these standings: a monthly close above $4,298 for Ethereum or $202 for Solana could erase those losses, while a monthly close below about $1.11 for XRP would erase its gains and completely alter the current balance.
XRP followed with a modest increase, rising from $1.11 to $1.33, a 19% gain that left the $1,000 stake worth $1,193.
So, which two coins lost money, and what should investors take away from this?
Bitcoin's messaging remained consistent as a digital store of value, while XRP faced scrutiny over the SEC's lawsuit against Ripple, the company linked to the token.
The value of a cryptocurrency ultimately depends on the price paid at the beginning just as much as on the network's developments over time.

passages: A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown.
The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.
A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server.

In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.
The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21.
Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin.
PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes.
Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.
The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell.
A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process.
That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million.

A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown. The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier. The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin. Donations subsequently increased the pot to 0.02511679 BTC, worth $2,021.22 at the time of the win. The creator's website recorded the successful claim at 15:47 UTC on October 25, after the challenge had been running for approximately 19.28 hours. The experiment follows the disclosure of CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, two critical PHP vulnerabilities that can allow remote code execution under certain conditions. The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21. Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server. The challenge's creator, posting under the name ‘cloudlandsdev’, had said the project was designed to see whether anyone could use the vulnerabilities to compromise the server and claim its Bitcoin. “Made this because I'm curious if anyone out there has figured out how to actually use this PHP RCE, we spent the last few days panicking. Have fun!” the creator wrote. PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes. Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account. The experiment quickly attracted attention, but the resulting traffic also became a problem. In an update, the creator said visitors were exhausting the server's available computing resources shortly after each capacity increase. Limited storage also prevented the server from retaining all its logs, complicating efforts to document a successful attempt. The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition. Subsequent requests then exposed memory contents through session cookies, providing information about the locations of PHP's memory structures and executable code. Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup. The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process. Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address. However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet. Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server. In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password. The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable. They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million. Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024. A more recent case involved a Bitcoin holder who r ecovered five BTC worth roughly $400,000 in May 2026 after losing access to the wallet for years. The pseudonymous owner, known as ‘cprkrn’, said Anthropic's Claude AI helped identify a backup file from December 2019, which could be decrypted using a password the owner had previously written down in a notebook. The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin. The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell. A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process. That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all. The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition.
The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable.
They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million.
Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024.
The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin.
Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup.
The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process.

Stealmybitcoin.com, the site where the game was hosted, verified the bounty had been claimed.

sources.title: $2,000 Bitcoin bounty challenge may be impossible to crack due to server setup doubts.
passages: The story about a website daring hackers to steal Bitcoin offers a $2,000 prize but remains unclaimed after over 17 hours.
An independent analysis suggests the server configuration might prevent the advertised PHP2Shell exploit from being accessible, possibly making the challenge unsolvable.
While the PHP flaws are real and require patching, the challenge’s setup raises questions about whether the competition is fair or rigged.

coreStoryFacts.text: A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown.
The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.
A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server.

In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.
The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21.
Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin.
PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes.
Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.
The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell.
A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process.
That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment.

The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition.

The experiment came days after a scramble over two critical bugs in PHP.
Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online, prompting PHP’s maintainers to ship emergency fixes on October 21, a day ahead of schedule, as Cryptopolitan reported.

While the PHP flaws are real and require patching, the challenge’s setup raises questions about whether the competition is fair or rigged.

A security researcher was able to exploit an intentionally unpatched PHP server and claim its Bitcoin bounty in just over 19 hours.
The page reads: “For now, there are no bitcoin on this server,” adding that more challenges may follow.
The experiment came days after a scramble over two critical bugs in PHP.
Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online, prompting PHP’s maintainers to ship emergency fixes on October 21, a day ahead of schedule, as Cryptopolitan reported.
Stealmybitcoin.com, the site where the game was hosted, verified the bounty had been claimed.
Its results page shows the Bitcoin was taken after 19.28 hours, with the win being logged at 15:47 UTC on Sunday, October 25.
Randa Moses is an editor and reporter at Cryptopolitan covering tech, AI, robotics, crypto, scams, and hacks.
She has worked in the crypto space since 2017.
She held roles at Forward Protocol, AmaZix, and Cryptosomniac.
Randa holds a degree in Electrical and Electronics Engineering from the University of Bradford.
The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and dubbed PHP2Shell, both received a severity score of 9.2 out of 10 and enable remote code execution on unpatched servers.
The public stunt was a test to see if the recent PHP2Shell flaws are as dangerous as they are said to be.
The story about a website daring hackers to steal Bitcoin offers a $2,000 prize but remains unclaimed after over 17 hours.
An independent analysis suggests the server configuration might prevent the advertised PHP2Shell exploit from being accessible, possibly making the challenge unsolvable.
While the PHP flaws are real and require patching, the challenge’s setup raises questions about whether the competition is fair or rigged.

The winner, ‘KillaBoi’, published a proof of concept on GitHub describing the attack against the live challenge and providing a local test environment.

The exploit took advantage of PHP's handling of multipart uploads and session data, where, by pushing a PHP worker beyond its memory limit, the attacker could leave internal state in an inconsistent condition.
The researchers reverse-engineered an older version of RoboForm's password generator and identified a flaw that made the password predictable.
They recovered the wallet in November 2023, when the Bitcoin was worth approximately $1.6 million.
Its value had climbed to nearly $3 million by the time the recovery was reported in May 2024.
The backup contained the keys needed to access the Bitcoin.
Notably, the attacker used those addresses to construct a forged PHP data structure that triggered command execution during cleanup.
The final request returned evidence that the command had run inside the PHP process.
Although the server was successfully compromised, the recovered private key did not match the advertised prize address.
However, on-chain data shows the funds were subsequently sent to an address “bc1qr4…lk7a9” , labeled as a Kraken cold wallet.

passages: A security researcher was able to exploit an intentionally unpatched PHP server and claim its Bitcoin bounty in just over 19 hours.

The experiment came days after a scramble over two critical bugs in PHP.
Details of the vulnerabilities leaked online, prompting PHP’s maintainers to ship emergency fixes on October 21, a day ahead of schedule, as Cryptopolitan reported.
Stealmybitcoin.com, the site where the game was hosted, verified the bounty had been claimed.
Its results page shows the Bitcoin was taken after 19.28 hours, with the win being logged at 15:47 UTC on Sunday, October 25.

story.title: Bitcoin reward offered to anyone who could break into an unpatched server running PHP, hacker cracks site and claims bounty — PHP2Shell challenge tested claims that AI makes exploiting vulnerabilities easy - Tom's Hardware

facts.text: A hacker has successfully breached a vulnerable server, claiming a prize pot worth $2,021.22 in Bitcoin after exploiting PHP2Shell vulnerabilities, a posting on the Steal My Bitcoin website has shown.
The challenge's creator confirmed the win on October 25, ending an experiment designed to test claims that exploiting critical software vulnerabilities is becoming easier.
A Bitcoin hacking challenge is daring security researchers to exploit critical PHP vulnerabilities and steal the cryptocurrency, putting claims about real-world exploitability to the test.
Bitcoin recovery efforts have previously involved reverse-engineering software rather than exploiting a live server.

In 2024, hardware hacker Joe Grand, known as ‘Kingpin”, and researcher Bruno recovered access to 43.6 BTC belonging to an owner identified as Michael, who had forgotten a 20-character wallet password.
The flaws received critical severity ratings, and fixes were released on October 21.
Turning the vulnerabilities into a reliable attack, however, requires more than simply running a publicly available exploit against an arbitrary server.
Tom's Hardware is part of Future US Inc, an international media group and leading digital publisher.
The challenge, hosted on the website a day earlier and announced through a forum post , initially offered approximately $502 worth of Bitcoin.
PHP2Shell refers to two vulnerabilities in PHP’s request-handling and memory-management processes.
Under vulnerable configurations, an attacker could potentially exploit these flaws to execute code with the privileges of the web server account.
The latest event comes as security teams face pressure to patch PHP installations following the public disclosure of PHP2Shell.
A separate report on the vulnerability disclosure controversy detailed how premature publication disrupted the coordinated release process.
That said, for now, evidence of the latest successful attack suggests that exploiting these PHP vulnerabilities may not be that hard after all.

extraction.body: TODD BREASSEALE: Hey, good afternoon, everyone. Today we're going to discuss the Defense Intelligence Agency's release of its latest, unclassified, foundational report, “Challenges to Security in Space 2022.” This is the second edition of DIA’s series of reports designed to inform the public on key challenges and foreign military threats in space. DIA’s foundational reports foster informed dialogues between America's leaders, the national security community, warfighters, academia, allies and partners about key national security challenges facing the United States. We're joined today by DIA’s foremost experts in the space field, Dr. John Huth, DIA’s Defense Intelligence Officer for Space and Counterspace, and Mr. Kevin Ryder DIA Senior Defense Intelligence Analyst for Space and Counterspace. Gentlemen, I'll hand it over to you. DEFENSE INTELLIGENCE OFFICER DR. JOHN F. HUTH: Thank you for the opportunity to discuss DIA’s report that we're releasing today, “Challenges to Security in Space 2022.” This is an unclassified report and it's a follow-on to the first “Challenges to Security in Space” DIA released in 2019. Like its predecessor, this report examines the space and counterspace programs that pose or potentially pose a significant challenge to U.S. or partner interests by China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran. The second iteration addresses increases in the pace and scope of competitive space operations since early 2019, which you're about to hear have been dramatic. DIA produces reports that provide both broad overviews of country military capabilities known as the Military Power Series, and more narrowly focused functional threat reports such as “Challenges to Security in Space” and “Global Nuclear Landscapes.” These are designed to help the public achieve a deeper understanding of key challenges and threats to U.S. national security. This new edition of “Challenges to Security in Space” provides an updated unclassified overview of current threats to U.S. space-based capabilities. Particularly from China and Russia, but also to a lesser extent, those emerging from North Korea and Iran. This edition examines the expansion of space operations and details Earth-focused space services, as well as growing efforts to explore the moon and beyond. And it also includes an expanded assessment of impacts of space debris. Space-based capabilities impact many day-to-day aspects of the American way of life. They enable functions that affect our homes, transportation, electric power grids, banking and communications. From watching television, to predicting weather patterns to avoiding traffic on our daily commutes, satellites enable many real-time conveniences that have become integral to our daily lives. On the national security front, space-based capabilities afford the United States and our allies with crucial ability to project combat power to areas of conflict and instability. They enable our armed forces to collect vital intelligence on foreign threats, navigate and maneuver rapidly, and communicate with one another to support global military and humanitarian crises. Meanwhile, Russia and China, our primary strategic competitors, are taking steps to undercut the United States and our allies in the space domain. Both nations view space as a requirement for winning modern wars, especially against Western nations, and look to prove themselves as world leaders. Since early 2019, competitor space operations have increased in pace and scope across nearly all major categories — communications, remote sensing, navigation, and science and technology demonstration. SENIOR DEFENSE ANALYST KEVIN RYDER: And China and Russia value superiority in space. And as a result, they'll seek ways to strengthen their space and counter-space programs and determine better ways to integrate them within their respective militaries. Both nations seek to broaden their space exploration initiatives together and individually with plans to explore the moon and Mars during the next 30 years. And if successful, these efforts will likely lead to attempts by Beijing and Moscow to exploit the moon's natural resources. Beijing and Moscow have integrated space-based capabilities into their individual, national and warfighting strategies with the intent of denying the United States a space-enabled advantage. Evidence of both nations’ intent to undercut the United States and allied leadership in the space domain can be seen in the growth of combined in-orbit assets of China and Russia, which grew approximately 70% in just two years. This recent and continuing expansion follows a more than 200% increase between 2015 and 2018. China has launched a robotic lander and rover to the far side of the moon, and an orbiter lander and rover in one mission to Mars. It has also launched multiple missiles, capable of destroying satellites, and deployed mobile jammers to deny satellite communications and GPS. Moscow on the other hand, has developed a suite of counter-space weapons capabilities, including electronic warfare, to deny, degrade, and disrupt communications, and to not - to deny the use of space-based imagery. Russia is also developing a mobile missile that is able to destroy satellites and crewed space vehicles. Now as the number of spacefaring nations grow, and counter-space capabilities become more integrated into military operations, the U.S. Space Posture will be increasingly challenged and orbit assets will face new risk. A secure, stable, and accessible space domain is crucial as challenges to the United States and our allies’ space capabilities continue to increase. “Challenges to Security in Space — 2022” offs the insights from top intelligence experts on current threats to the United States Space Posture posed by our strategic competitors, and key space issues through 2030 and beyond. Thank you for your time, we will now take questions. MR. BREASSEALE: So, if you have a question for these gentlemen, please just raise your hand and I'll call on you. And you can please state your name and outlet for which you're reporting. I saw your hand first. Yes, ma'am. Q: Hi, Tara Copp with Defense One. I was wondering if you could both talk about the extent to which China has been watching Russia's invasion of Ukraine and how it's shaping what counter-space capabilities it's pursuing? And what sort of - is it gathering lessons learned? Will it make it more difficult in future conflicts based on what we've seen happen over Ukraine? DR. HUTH: So, as far as the scope of the document really doesn't cover that, that's fairly new, and I’ll say, evolving information. So, really don't have a whole lot to – to add on that right now. MR. RYDER: So, I will say that, from a DIA perspective, what we do is we provide information on the threats and the challenges that are posed by our adversaries. And we provide that to our policymakers and our warfighting planners to make those determinations on the type of systems and mitigation strategies that are needed. DR. HUTH: And certainly, the acquisition community, the NRO [National Reconnaissance Office], SDA – Space Development Agency, et cetera. But as Kevin said, that's really for us to inform them. It's for them to figure out, based on that threat information, what they want to do. MR. BREASSEALE: Let’s take a caller, Theresa Hitchens, from Breaking Defense. MR. BREASSEALE: I want to go to the phones real quickly. Bill Gertz, Washington Times. Q: Yes. Hi. I want to follow up on Tony's question on the fractional orbital launch. Can you say whether this is a nuclear system, or it's a conventional system? And it is reported in the report as part of space weapons that are used to hit targets on the earth, on the sea and in the air. Can you elaborate a little bit more on that? MR. RYDER: Could you repeat the question? I'm sorry. And I know, Ukraine happened after this is published, but to the extent that that is occurring on the current battlefield, what sort of guidance are you providing, or helping shape future U.S. defenses for future potential conflict? DR. HUTH: So again, I'd say the report, and the information from an intelligence perspective stands as it is. So those types of things are what we provide to our customers, for them to consider as they are acquiring new capabilities with the understanding that both China and Russia are expanding their kit, if you will, in counter-space capabilities. And those are all factored into design of U.S. systems. MR. BREASSEALE: Let's go to the phones again. Poonam Sharma from Global Straits. MR. RYDER: So, from my perspective, all of the capabilities are equal in nature. It depends on how and why and when the adversary would tend to use them or choose to use them. DR. HUTH: And if I could just reemphasize my last point and pile on what Kevin said. So, it's not just a capability, it's the fact that they have a space force or each have space forces, China and Russia. And their intent is to make space part of that combined arms effort in any conflict. Q: Can I follow up on that a little bit, on John's question? Which capability are they the most advanced in, that's the most alarming to you? Q: Thank you so much. Just a couple of short questions. Does DIA also produce a classified version of this report or just the unclassified? And the second part of the question, in your discussion on China's capabilities, do you consider all Chinese space capabilities military? Or do you make a distinction between civilian space and military space? Thank you. MR. RYDER: So, for your first question, while DIA does publish a number of classified documents, “Challenges to Security in Space” is only produced in an unclassified format. DR. HUTH: I think with regard to your second question, Kevin, and I think I, had already both talked about what the Chinese refer to as civil-military fusion. So sometimes, things can look very distinct as to whether they lay on one side or another, at least for the time being. And that can change because of that, and there's a lot of gray area in there. They - they don't conduct business the way - certainly the way the U.S. or other Western countries do. Q: Hi, I'm Luis Martinez with ABC News. I have two questions. One, how does - in terms of the counter-space activities we're seeing from Russia and China, how does this report compare with what the conclusions from the 2019 report? You know, broad strokes, what's the main difference between those two? MR. RYDER: Well, as you said, 2022 builds on our 2019 report. It expands a little bit more on some of the future developments. It also takes a harder look at space debris and the causes - the potential impact of that in space. And it also looks at development to get out - exploration out beyond the moon. DR. HUTH: And I think we go a little bit deeper on space domain awareness and command and control as well in the new report.

And it also includes an expanded assessment of impacts of space debris.

Space-based capabilities impact many day-to-day aspects of the American way of life. They enable functions that affect our homes, transportation, electric power grids, banking and communications. From watching television, to predicting weather patterns to avoiding traffic on our daily commutes, satellites enable many real-time conveniences that have become integral to our daily lives. On the national security front, space-based capabilities afford the United States and our allies with crucial ability to project combat power to areas of conflict and instability. They enable our armed forces to collect vital intelligence on foreign threats, navigate and maneuver rapidly, and communicate with one another to support global military and humanitarian crises.

Meanwhile, Russia and China, our primary strategic competitors, are taking steps to undercut the United States and our allies in the space domain. Both nations view space as a requirement for winning modern wars, especially against Western nations, and look to prove themselves as world leaders.

Since early 2019, competitor space operations have increased in pace and scope across nearly all major categories — communications, remote sensing, navigation, and science and technology demonstration.

SENIOR DEFENSE ANALYST KEVIN RYDER: And China and Russia value superiority in space. And as a result, they'll seek ways to strengthen their space and counter-space programs and determine better ways to integrate them within their respective militaries. Both nations seek to broaden their space exploration initiatives together and individually with plans to explore the moon and Mars during the next 30 years.

And if successful, these efforts will likely lead to attempts by Beijing and Moscow to exploit the moon's natural resources. Beijing and Moscow have integrated space-based capabilities into their individual, national and warfighting strategies with the intent of denying the United States a space-enabled advantage.

Evidence of both nations’ intent to undercut the United States and allied leadership in the space domain can be seen in the growth of combined in-orbit assets of China and Russia, which grew approximately 70% in just two years. This recent and continuing expansion follows a more than 200% increase between 2015 and 2018.

China has launched a robotic lander and rover to the far side of the moon, and an orbiter lander and rover in one mission to Mars. It has also launched multiple missiles, capable of destroying satellites, and deployed mobile jammers to deny satellite communications and GPS. Moscow on the other hand, has developed a suite of counter-space weapons capabilities, including electronic warfare, to deny, degrade, and disrupt communications, and to not - to deny the use of space-based imagery.

Russia is also developing a mobile missile that is able to destroy satellites and crewed space vehicles. Now as the number of spacefaring nations grow, and counter-space capabilities become more integrated into military operations, the U.S. Space Posture will be increasingly challenged and orbit assets will face new risk. A secure, stable, and accessible space domain is crucial as challenges to the United States and our allies’ space capabilities continue to increase.

“Challenges to Security in Space — 2022” offs the insights from top intelligence experts on current threats to the United States Space Posture posed by our strategic competitors, and key space issues through 2030 and beyond. Thank you for your time, we will now take questions.

MR. BREASSEALE: So, if you have a question for these gentlemen, please just raise your hand and I'll call on you. And you can please state your name and outlet for which you're reporting. I saw your hand first. Yes, ma'am.

Q: Hi, Tara Copp with Defense One. I was wondering if you could both talk about the extent to which China has been watching Russia's invasion of Ukraine and how it's shaping what counter-space capabilities it's pursuing? And what sort of - is it gathering lessons learned? Will it make it more difficult in future conflicts based on what we've seen happen over Ukraine?
DR. HUTH: So, as far as the scope of the document really doesn't cover that, that's fairly new, and I’ll say, evolving information. So, really don't have a whole lot to – to add on that right now.

MR. RYDER: So, I will say that, from a DIA perspective, what we do is we provide information on the threats and the challenges that are posed by our adversaries. And we provide that to our policymakers and our warfighting planners to make those determinations on the type of systems and mitigation strategies that are needed.

DR. HUTH: And certainly, the acquisition community, the NRO [National Reconnaissance Office], SDA – Space Development Agency, et cetera. But as Kevin said, that's really for us to inform them. It's for them to figure out, based on that threat information, what they want to do.
MR. BREASSEALE: Let’s take a caller, Theresa Hitchens, from Breaking Defense.
MR. BREASSEALE: I want to go to the phones real quickly. Bill Gertz, Washington Times.

Q: Yes. Hi. I want to follow up on Tony's question on the fractional orbital launch. Can you say whether this is a nuclear system, or it's a conventional system? And it is reported in the report as part of space weapons that are used to hit targets on the earth, on the sea and in the air. Can you elaborate a little bit more on that?
MR. RYDER: Could you repeat the question? I'm sorry.

And I know, Ukraine happened after this is published, but to the extent that that is occurring on the current battlefield, what sort of guidance are you providing, or helping shape future U.S. defenses for future potential conflict?

DR. HUTH: So again, I'd say the report, and the information from an intelligence perspective stands as it is. So those types of things are what we provide to our customers, for them to consider as they are acquiring new capabilities with the understanding that both China and Russia are expanding their kit, if you will, in counter-space capabilities. And those are all factored into design of U.S. systems.
MR. BREASSEALE: Let's go to the phones again. Poonam Sharma from Global Straits.
MR. RYDER: So, from my perspective, all of the capabilities are equal in nature. It depends on how and why and when the adversary would tend to use them or choose to use them.

DR. HUTH: And if I could just reemphasize my last point and pile on what Kevin said. So, it's not just a capability, it's the fact that they have a space force or each have space forces, China and Russia. And their intent is to make space part of that combined arms effort in any conflict.
Q: Can I follow up on that a little bit, on John's question? Which capability are they the most advanced in, that's the most alarming to you?

Q: Thank you so much. Just a couple of short questions. Does DIA also produce a classified version of this report or just the unclassified? And the second part of the question, in your discussion on China's capabilities, do you consider all Chinese space capabilities military? Or do you make a distinction between civilian space and military space? Thank you.
MR. RYDER: So, for your first question, while DIA does publish a number of classified documents, “Challenges to Security in Space” is only produced in an unclassified format.

DR. HUTH: I think with regard to your second question, Kevin, and I think I, had already both talked about what the Chinese refer to as civil-military fusion. So sometimes, things can look very distinct as to whether they lay on one side or another, at least for the time being. And that can change because of that, and there's a lot of gray area in there. They - they don't conduct business the way - certainly the way the U.S. or other Western countries do.

Q: Hi, I'm Luis Martinez with ABC News. I have two questions. One, how does - in terms of the counter-space activities we're seeing from Russia and China, how does this report compare with what the conclusions from the 2019 report? You know, broad strokes, what's the main difference between those two?

MR. RYDER: Well, as you said, 2022 builds on our 2019 report. It expands a little bit more on some of the future developments.
